articles.title: New study suggests possible connection between GLP-1s and hair loss in men
articles.summary: Hair loss has become one of the most reported concerns among people taking GLP-1 drugs, such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Zepbound - so much so that the phenomenon...
articles.body:
Hair loss has become one of the most reported concerns among people taking GLP-1 drugs, such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Zepbound - so much so that the phenomenon has earned the nickname "Ozempic hair."

Several studies have investigated whether these drugs are linked to hair loss, but none has shown that the medications themselves cause hair to fall out. Now, new research offers a clue about a possible biological connection between GLP-1s and thinning hair - at least in men.

In the study, published in the Journal of Investigative Dermatology, researchers at NYU Langone Health found a link between higher levels of the GLP-1 receptor in the blood and male-pattern hair loss. The finding doesn't mean that men who take GLP-1s will definitely develop male pattern hair loss, but it suggests that these medications could be contributing to what people are observing.

Here's what we know - and don't know - about the connection between GLP-1 drugs and hair loss.

When you eat, your body naturally releases GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1), a hormone that attaches to GLP-1 receptors (proteins located on the surface of many cells) throughout the body and communicates that it's time to slow digestion, release insulin and feel full. GLP-1 drugs work by mimicking this hormone.

For this study, the researchers looked at people with genetic variants associated with naturally higher levels of GLP-1 receptors, which means their cells may have a greater response to the hormone. Then they looked through a genetic database to see whether those variants were linked to men with male-pattern hair loss - which typically causes a receding hairline, thinning at the temples and a bald spot at the crown of the head.

They found that higher GLP-1 activity was associated with about 7 percent greater odds of male-pattern hair loss, suggesting that the two may be biologically related, said senior study author Lynn Petukhova, an assistant professor in the Ronald O. Perelman Department of Dermatology and the Department of Population Health at NYU Grossman School of Medicine.

The findings build on a study published earlier this year that found a slight increase in the risk of hair loss in people with Type 2 diabetes taking GLP-1 drugs compared with other types of diabetes drugs. But there's an important caveat with the NYU study: None of the subjects were actually taking a GLP-1 medication.

That means that while the study suggests a connection between having greater GLP-1 receptor activity and male-pattern hair loss, it doesn't tell us whether people taking GLP-1s are more likely to have hair loss.

"Genetic association does not equal drug effect," said Justin Ko, chief of dermatology at Stanford Health Care, who specializes in hair loss and was not involved in the research. "It is suggestive evidence, but I don't think we can say this is a causal effect."

Another limitation of the study is that it was largely made up of men of European ancestry, so it's not clear whether the results apply to other populations.

The new study may point to a potential biological connection, but it doesn't explain why so many people report hair loss after starting a GLP-1 drug.

Carolyn Goh, a clinical professor of dermatology at UCLA Health, who was not involved in the study, says she frequently sees hair shedding in patients taking GLP-1s. But, she added, it's difficult to pinpoint what's causing it.

"It could be the medication, it could be the weight loss, it could be metabolic changes, it could be insufficient nutrition," she said. "There are a lot of different things that could be going on."

It's well documented that rapid weight loss of any kind - whether from GLP-1s, bariatric surgery or crash dieting - can stress the body and lead to hair loss, Ko said. This type of hair loss is called telogen effluvium.

Hair typically goes through different cycles of rest and growth. With telogen effluvium, more hair follicles than usual enter a resting phase at the same time. (It's one way your body tries to conserve energy during times of stress, Petukhova said.) Those hairs eventually shed, causing noticeable thinning. Unlike male-pattern hair loss, which causes a patchy type of balding, this shedding tends to be diffuse, meaning hair comes out from all over the scalp.

A significant drop in calories can also make it harder to get enough of the nutrients that are essential for hair growth. A lack of protein and calcium, folate, B12 and iron, for example, can contribute to hair shedding, Ko said.

Telogen effluvium typically doesn't start immediately after a stressful event. Hair follicles can take weeks to respond, so shedding often begins about two to three months after the stressor. That delay can make it difficult for someone to know whether their hair loss is related to weight loss, nutritional deficiencies or something else entirely unrelated that happened months earlier.

A period of intense shedding may also make underlying hair loss more noticeable, Ko said. Male- and female-pattern hair loss is extremely common and develops gradually. A person may already have the genetic tendency toward it without realizing it. Then, a bout of telogen effluvium makes this hair loss more pronounced, Ko said.

What to do if you're worried about hair loss

If you're taking a GLP-1 drug, talk with your health care team to make sure you're getting enough protein and other nutrients. (It's critical for maintaining muscle and bone mass, too.) Ko also recommended talking with your doctor about whether you're losing weight too fast. In some cases, slowing it down may reduce the physical stress that can trigger shedding, he said.

If you do notice more hair in your brush or shower drain, it doesn't mean that the medication is permanently damaging your hair.

For most people, telogen effluvium after weight loss is temporary. As the body adjusts to its new weight and nutritional intake stabilizes, the hair cycle will return to normal and the hair can regrow, Ko said. It does take time, though: "You're going to see your hair coming back and regrowing over the course of the next six to 12 months," he said.

If your hair loss continues for more than about six months, Goh suggests seeing a dermatologist, particularly one who specializes in hair loss. They can examine your scalp and determine whether you're dealing with telogen effluvium, pattern hair loss or another condition.

The distinction matters, because some hair loss can be treated with medications such as minoxidil or finasteride, Goh said. You should see a dermatologist right away if you develop clear bald patches, significant scalp inflammation or a rash or symptoms such as pain, itching or scaling. Loss of eyebrows or eyelashes also can signal a type of hair-loss condition that warrants evaluation, Goh said.

What this study means if you're considering a GLP-1

The new study adds to an area of research that is still unsettled. Goh said she wouldn't dismiss hair loss as a possible consideration for someone deciding whether to take a GLP-1. But she also wouldn't view the study's 7 percent increase in odds of male-pattern hair loss as a reason on its own to avoid a medication that may provide important health benefits.

"It's definitely a patient-centered conversation," she said. The same potential side effect may matter very differently to two people depending on how much they need or want the medication and how concerned they are about hair loss, she said.

Ko agreed that the study shouldn't be interpreted as evidence that people taking GLP-1 drugs should expect to lose their hair. The more immediate and established explanation for shedding after substantial weight loss is telogen effluvium, he said.

More research is needed to determine whether the study's genetic finding applies to people actually taking GLP-1 medications, women, and more diverse populations.

For now, experts say the message for people taking these medications is less about expecting hair loss and more about paying attention to what kind of hair loss is happening - and getting it evaluated if it persists or looks unusual.
authors: Jennifer Fields, Special to The Washington Post

articles.title: Esposa de Maduro tem problema cardíaco 'muito delicado', diz agência | G1
articles.standfirst: Informação foi dada pelo filho à agência France Presse. Cilia Flores foi presa junto com o marido durante uma operação dos Estados Unidos na Venezuela, no início do ano.
articles.summary: Informação foi dada pelo filho à agência France Presse. Cilia Flores foi presa junto com o marido durante uma operação dos Estados Unidos na Venezuela, no início do ano.
articles.body:
Maduro e a esposa Cilia Flores durante cerimônia de posse em Caracas, na Venezuela, em 10 de janeiro de 2025 — Foto: Reuters/Leonardo Fernandez Viloria

A esposa de Nicolás Maduro , que foi presa com o marido durante uma operação militar dos Estados Unidos na Venezuela, tem um problema cardíaco "muito delicado", disse o filho de Maduro à AFP.

Maduro foi detido pelas forças americanas durante uma incursão militar em 3 de janeiro, que incluiu bombardeios a Caracas .

A esposa, Cilia Flores, foi detida na mesma operação, em uma prisão de segurança máxima no Brooklyn. Ela é acusada por Washington por tráfico de drogas.

Segundo o advogado do casal, Mark Donnelly, Flores "estava fisicamente saudável e não tomava nenhum medicamento de forma contínua, exceto por uma injeção mensal" antes do sequestro.

Cilia toma quatro medicamentos e os problemas cardíacos requerem intervenção médica.

Atualmente, a ex-primeira-dama de 69 anos se encontra presa num centro de detenção federal no Brooklyn, em Nova York.

Alegando que as condições atuais de sua prisão a impedem de receber cuidados adequados, seu advogado solicita que ela seja colocada em prisão domiciliar nos Estados Unidos sob um regime rigoroso: vigilância armada 24 horas por dia, tornozeleira eletrônica e confisco de seu passaporte.

O ex-presidente venezuelano e sua esposa são acusados ​​de auxiliar no tráfico de cocaína para os Estados Unidos. Eles negam as acusações.

Desde a deposição de Maduro, sua ex-vice-presidente, Delcy Rodríguez, governa a Venezuela interinamente, sob intensa pressão de Washington.

articles.title: Avião militar cai na Nigéria com 32 pessoas a bordo em missão | G1
articles.standfirst: Avião realizava uma 'missão de rotina' entre o Benin, no sul do país, e Lagos, capital econômica, quando caiu.
articles.summary: Avião militar cai na Nigéria com 32 pessoas a bordo durante missão entre Benin City e Lagos, mobilizando equipes de resgate no estado de Ondo.
articles.body:
Avião ATR-42, da Força Aérea Nigeriana, que caiu nesta segunda-feira (5). — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo

Um avião da Força Aérea nigeriana caiu, nesta segunda-feira (5), no estado de Ondo, no sudoeste da Nigéria, com 32 pessoas a bordo, segundo o Exército e o ministro da Aviação.

O porta-voz da Força Aérea, Ehimen Ejodame, declarou que o avião realizava uma "missão de rotina" de Benin City, no sul do país, para Lagos, a capital econômica, quando caiu em Igbokoda, no estado de Ondo.

"As informações preliminares indicam que havia 25 passageiros e 7 tripulantes a bordo", declarou no X o ministro Festus Keyamo.

Keyamo acrescentou que o fuselagem do avião foi localizada, após cair perto de uma base naval.

Um vídeo divulgado nas redes sociais mostrava um grupo de pessoas à beira de um rio enquanto as equipes de resgate faziam buscas na área a partir de uma embarcação.

"As operações de busca e resgate, em coordenação com as autoridades competentes e os serviços de emergência, estão atualmente em curso", declarou Ejodame.

articles.title: É #FATO:Pane elétrica atrasou funcionamento de urna em Barra do Mendes | G1
articles.standfirst: Em nota, Justiça eleitoral informou: 'Ocorrência durou menos de uma hora; após atendimento técnico, votação seguiu e foi encerrada às 17h'.
articles.summary: Em vídeo viral, mulher denuncia problema. Justiça eleitoral explica que o local ficou sem funcionamento por menos de uma hora.
articles.body:
É #FATO que problema na rede elétrica atrasou funcionamento de urna em Barra do Mendes, na Bahia — Foto: Reprodução

Circula nas redes sociais o vídeo de uma mulher reclamando que uma urna eletrônica em Barra do Mendes , na Bahia, teve problemas de funcionamento durante a votação do primeiro turno das eleições 2026, neste domingo (4). É #FATO .

Publicado neste domingo no Instagram, onde teve mais de 48 mil curtidas, o vídeo mostra servidores tentando colocar em funcionamento uma urna eletrônica.

Na gravação, uma mulher afirma: "Estamos aqui na comunidade Morro do Gomes, na seção 176. A votação era para começar às 8 horas e estamos aqui, ó, com problema nas tomadas. Problema nas tomadas, aparece as coisas na urna e some . [...] Não aparece ninguém aqui, ó, para dar um auxílio, só o pessoal que vem entregar as urnas. Era bem feito voltar vazia, para assim vocês de uma vez aprender. [...] A tomada não presta. Viu?" .

Ela continua: "Já são oito, oito e quanto aí, amiga? Olha. As pessoas idosas têm a decência de vir aqui e exercer sua cidadania e chegam e acham uma esculhambação dessa [...]".

Na seção de comentários do post, usuários escreveram mensagens colocando em dúvida a lisura do processo eleitoral. Veja três exemplos: "Olha aí o golpe" ; "Começou a maracutaia né" ; e "Fecha a sala …. Denuncia picaretagem".

No final da noite deste domingo, a Justiça Eleitoral divulgou um comunicado com o seguinte título: "Problema na rede elétrica de local de votação em Barra do Mendes foi resolvido e eleitores votaram normalmente" . "

O texto descreve que o incidente ocorreu durou menos de uma área e ocorreu em uma área sob responsabilidade da 176ª Zona Eleitoral: "Um vídeo relata dificuldades no início da votação em um local identificado pela autora como situado na comunidade Morro Gomes, em Barra do Mendes (BA). Segundo o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral da Bahia (TRE-BA), foram constatados problemas na rede elétrica, solucionados com atendimento técnico e uso de estabilizadores de energia [...]. De acordo com o TRE-BA, o encerramento ocorreu às 17h, no horário previsto" .

De acordo com a Justiça Eleitoral, "a gravação apresenta reclamações durante a espera, mas não informa o desfecho da ocorrência" e "as equipes técnicas compareceram ao local, adotaram as providências necessárias e a votação teve continuidade".

Ainda segundo a nota, "o relato não demonstra falha no registro ou na contabilização dos votos".

articles.title: Pesquisadora de peste na Sibéria morre por causa desconhecida | G1
articles.standfirst: Autoridades afirmaram que mulher contraiu pneumonia. Ela trabalhava em instituto que pesquisa a peste na Sibéria, mas médicos disseram não ter encontrado relação. Ainda assim, caso gerou temor generalizado na Rússia de que doença, transmissível pelo ar, se espalhe pelo país.
articles.summary: A Rússia colocou um hospital inteiro em quarentena após uma funcionária de um instituto de pesquisa da peste na Sibéria morrer por causas desconhecidas.
articles.body:
Pesquisadores trabalham em laboratório do Instituto Irkutsk de Pesquisa Antipraga da Sibéria e do Oriente, em imagem de 2019. — Foto: Instituto Irkutsk de Pesquisa Antipraga da Sibéria e do Oriente via AP

A Rússia colocou um hospital inteiro em quarentena após uma funcionária de um instituto de pesquisa da peste na Sibéria morrer por causas desconhecidas .

O mistério fez com que autoridades colocassem o hospital em que a pesquisadora esteve internada em quarentena para investigar as casuas. E gerou uma onda de temor na Rússia de que a peste possa estar se espalhando pelo país .

Agentes de saúde também estão monitorando pessoas com quem a pesquisadora manteve contato.

Segundo a rede de TV estatal local, a mulher morreu na semana passada após contrair pneumonia de causa "desconhecida". As autoridades russas afirmaram não ter encontrado evidências de que a doença tenha sido causada por qualquer um dos patógenos com os quais a pesquisadora trabalhava .

No entanto, o caso gerou alerta na Rússia após relatos não confirmados na mídia sugerirem que ela poderia ter morrido de peste pneumônica — uma forma menos comum, porém grave, da doença, que pode ser transmitida de pessoa para pessoa .

A mulher trabalhava no Instituto de Pesquisa Antipeste da Sibéria e do Extremo Oriente, em Irkutsk, no sudeste da Sibéria. Uma emissora de TV estatal de Irkutsk noticiou na segunda-feira (5) que ela morreu na semana passada em um hospital em Shelekhov, uma cidade nos arredores de Irkutsk.

O hospital foi colocado em quarentena , disse o prefeito Maxim Modin na sexta-feira (2); a unidade não está mais admitindo nem dando alta a pacientes, e seu laboratório suspendeu a realização de exames de rotina. O ambulatório do hospital continuou funcionando normalmente, segundo ele.

Anna Popova, chefe da agência de vigilância sanitária da Rússia, a Rospotrebnadzor, viajou para Irkutsk e reuniu-se com o governador Igor Kobzev e outras autoridades na sexta-feira (2).

Kobzev afirmou que todas as pessoas que tiveram contato com a mulher estão sob supervisão médica. Ele não especificou a infecção, classificando o caso como suspeita de "uma infecção particularmente perigosa".

A Rospotrebnadzor estava implementando "uma gama completa de medidas antiepidêmicas", acrescentou ele.

A Rospotrebnadzor informou no domingo (4) que a mulher foi diagnosticada com "pneumonia de etiologia [origem] desconhecida" e declarou que testes "extensos" não detectaram "nenhum microrganismo associado às atividades profissionais da paciente".

A agência também afirmou não ter encontrado incidentes no instituto "envolvendo microrganismos patogênicos".

Duas pessoas que tiveram contato com a mulher testaram positivo para um vírus causador de resfriado comum, e outras duas, para Covid-19, informou a agência, acrescentando que os demais testados apresentaram resultados negativos.

Vista do Centro de Assistência Médica e Resgate, na região de Irkutsk, na Rússia, em 5 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Reuters

O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, disse na segunda-feira que não acredita haver motivo para alarme, mas que os EUA estão acompanhando o caso de perto, cientes de que ele "poderia se espalhar rapidamente", apesar da quarentena e de outros protocolos de saúde pública.

O veículo de notícias local independente Lyudi Baikala citou fontes não identificadas afirmando que o técnico de laboratório, de 28 anos, morreu de peste pneumônica e que vários hospitais de Irkutsk foram colocados em quarentena.

Questionado na segunda-feira sobre o caso, o porta-voz do Kremlin, Dmitry Peskov, disse que o público e a mídia devem acompanhar os comunicados oficiais do Rospotrebnadzor, em vez de "rumores ou especulações".

O Rospotrebnadzor não havia se manifestado até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A Fábrica de Alumínio de Irkutsk, em Shelekhov, exigiu que os funcionários usassem máscaras como medida de precaução; o diretor da unidade, Artyom Fominykh, fez o anúncio no sábado pelo Telegram, pedindo calma e acrescentando: "É melhor prevenir do que remediar".

👉 A Organização Mundial da Saúde descreve a peste pneumônica como uma forma menos comum, porém grave, de peste — uma doença causada pela *Yersinia pestis*, bactéria geralmente encontrada em pequenos mamíferos e suas pulgas.

"No caso de uma possível exposição em laboratório, seria normal identificar os indivíduos que possam ter sido expostos e monitorá-los de acordo com o nível de risco avaliado", disse o Dr. Malick Gibani, professor clínico associado de vacinologia bacteriana no Imperial College London.

A escala de qualquer programa de monitoramento dependeria das "circunstâncias da exposição e do número de pessoas potencialmente afetadas", afirmou Gibani em um comentário por escrito.

Ian Jones, professor de virologia da Universidade de Reading, disse que "a peste carrega um histórico enorme e ainda está presente em muitas partes do mundo, incluindo a Rússia" , embora, devido às condições de vida modernas e aos antibióticos, "seu potencial seja, portanto, limitado" .

articles.title: Nikolas Ferreira: quem é o deputado federal mais votado do Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Neste domingo (4), mineiro de 30 anos foi reeleito com 3.118.784 votos, o maior número da história.
articles.summary: Nikolas Ferreira alcançou a maior votação da história do Brasil ao ser reeleito deputado federal com mais de 3,1 milhões de votos nestas eleições.
articles.body:
Deputado federal mais votado do país em duas eleições consecutivas, Nikolas Ferreira (PL) entrou na política há apenas seis anos e se tornou uma das principais lideranças da direita brasileira.

Criado na comunidade do Cabana do Pai Tomás, na Região Oeste de Belo Horizonte, Nikolas cresceu frequentando a igreja criada pelo pai, o pastor Edésio de Oliveira. No início da adolescência, morou na França com a família e, depois, retornou para a capital mineira e se formou em Direito pela PUC Minas.

Ele passou a se envolver em manifestações políticas e, em 2020, aos 24 anos, disputou uma eleição pela primeira vez, pelo PRTB. Foi o segundo vereador mais votado de BH , com 29.388 votos.

Na Câmara Municipal, foi autor do projeto de lei que proíbe o uso de linguagem neutra nas escolas . A proposta chegou a ser vetada pelo ex-prefeito Fuad Noman (PSD), mas o veto foi derrubado pelo Legislativo.

Em 2022, já no PL, Nikolas disputou uma vaga na Câmara dos Deputados e foi o mais votado do país , com 1.492.047 votos.

Desde então, ele se tornou uma das principais vozes da direita. Fenômeno nas redes sociais com mais de 22,6 milhões de seguidores, Nikolas é conhecido por fazer vídeos com temas conservadores e críticas à esquerda e a ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).

Nas eleições de 2026, aos 30 anos, casado e pai de duas meninas, foi reeleito neste domingo (4) com 3.118.784 votos, o maior número da história .

Nikolas também apoiou e ajudou a eleger diversos parlamentares pelo Brasil, inclusive Lucas Pavanato (PL), o deputado federal mais votado de São Paulo e o segundo mais votado do país.

articles.title: Dia das Crianças no Vale do Paraíba: vendas e preços em alta | G1
articles.standfirst: Expectativa é de crescimento de 3% nas vendas em outubro em comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado, segundo Sincovat.
articles.summary: O Dia das Crianças no Vale do Paraíba deve ter alta de 3% nas vendas, apesar do aumento de 7% no preço dos brinquedos e 11% em eletrônicos, segundo o Sincovat.
articles.body:
Dia das Crianças: comércio do Vale do Paraíba tem expectativa alta para vendas. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

O comércio do Vale do Paraíba e do Litoral Norte espera aumento nas vendas com a proximidade do Dia das Crianças, celebrado em 12 de outubro. A expectativa é de crescimento de cerca de 3% nas vendas em outubro, em comparação com o mesmo mês do ano passado.

O levantamento é do Sindicato do Comércio Varejista de Taubaté e região (Sincovat). Entre os produtos mais procurados para presentear estão brinquedos, calçados e roupas infantis. Calçados e roupas infantis também estão entre os itens que devem ter maior procura neste período.

Apesar da expectativa de aumento nas vendas, levantamento do Sincovat, com base em dados do Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA), mostra que os brinquedos estão 7% mais caros nos últimos 12 meses.

Quem pretende presentear com um produto de maior valor agregado, como é o caso do computador e de outros eletrônicos, vai pagar 11,38% a mais do que no ano passado. Por outro lado, o preço da bicicleta recuou 0,28%.

Quanto ao vestuário, os itens subiram abaixo da inflação. Como a camiseta, que está 0,11% mais cara, a bermuda, que registrou aumento de 2,91%, e a calça, que está custando 3,92% a mais do que no ano passado. O conjunto infantil teve queda de 1,09%.

Para atividades de lazer e turismo, os preços também subiram abaixo da inflação geral. O ingresso do cinema, teatro e concertos subiu 5,81%, o da hospedagem avançou 5,93%, enquanto o pacote turístico ficou 0,58% mais barato.

O Dia das Crianças acontece na próxima segunda-feira (12) e é uma das primeiras datas importantes para o comércio no último trimestre do ano, já que serve como termômetro para o final do ano. Na sequência, o varejo ainda se prepara para períodos de grande movimentação, como a Black Friday e o Natal.

articles.title: Câmara Municipal de SP tem nove vereadores eleitos deputados e terá nova composição em 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Seis parlamentares foram eleitos para a Câmara dos Deputados e três para a Alesp. Mudanças devem abrir espaço para suplentes e alterar a composição da Casa
articles.summary: Seis parlamentares foram eleitos para a Câmara dos Deputados e três para a Alesp. Mudanças devem abrir espaço para suplentes e alterar a composição da Casa
articles.body:
Plenário da Câmara Municipal de São Paulo. — Foto: Douglas Ferreira/Rede Câmara

Dos 24 vereadores de São Paulo que se candidataram a algum cargo, nove conseguiram se eleger deputados federais e estaduais na eleição deste domingo (4). Isso significa que deverão deixar a Câmara Municipal da capital paulista a partir do ano que vem e abrir espaço para os suplentes (veja lista completa abaixo) .

O maior destaque do pleito foi Lucas Pavanato (PL), que recebeu mais de 3 milhões de votos e se elegeu como o deputado federal mais votado da história de São Paulo . A marca só é comparável aos números do amigo Nikolas Ferreira (PL), que se reelegeu com 3,1 milhões de votos em Minas Gerais.

Outro vereador ficou entre os 10 deputados federais mais votados pelo eleitorado paulista. Na sexta colocação, o policial militar Sargento Nantes (PP) teve cerca de 333 mil votos, praticamente o triplo da votação conquistata em 2024, quando se elegeu para a Câmara Municipal.

Também tiveram votações expressivas as vereadoras Ana Carolina Oliveira (Podemos), com 246 mil votos, e Luna Zarattini (PT), com 233 mil votos. Ambas estiveram entre as vereadoras mais votadas quando se elegeram pela primeira vez e foram apostas de seus partidos para a eleição desse ano, que rendeu às duas praticamente o dobro dos votos conquistados em 2024.

Sandra Tadeu (PL) e Sidney Cruz (MDB), candidato apoiado pelo prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB), também conseguiram se eleger para a Câmara dos Deputados com mais de 100 mil votos cada. O vereador suplente em exercício Carlos Bezerra Júnior (PSD) também se elegeu deputado federal.

Na disputa pela Assembleia Legislativa de São Paulo (Alesp), três vereadores da capital conseguiram se eleger deputados estaduais: Thammy Miranda (PSD), Marina Bragante (PSB) e Keit Lima (PSOL).

A maioria dos vereadores candidatos, porém, não conseguiu repetir o sucesso eleitoral de 2024 . Entre os mais votados daquele pleito que não conseguiram um novo cargo está Rubinho Nunes (União). Depois de obter 101 mil votos na eleição à Câmara Municipal, dessa vez teve apenas 41 mil votos. Também não se elegeram nomes como Zoe Martínez (PL), que caiu de 60 mil para 25 mil votos, e Cris Monteiro (Novo), que caiu de 57 mil para 40 mil votos.

Os vereadores Lucas Pavanato, Sargento Nantes, Ana Carolina Oliveira e Luna Zarattini foram eleitos deputados federais — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram e Rede Câmara

A recomposição da Câmara Municipal, formada por 55 vereadores, dependerá da formalização das renúncias dos parlamentares eleitos e da convocação oficial dos suplentes. O cenário ainda pode sofrer alterações porque há vereadores licenciados e suplentes atualmente em exercício, o que afeta a ordem de substituição em algumas bancadas.

No PL, as saídas de Lucas Pavanato e Sandra Tadeu devem abrir espaço para Tenente Bahia e Tenente Nascimento. Primeiro suplente da legenda, o ex-lutador de MMA Felipe Sertanejo, não assumirá uma cadeira na Câmara Municipal porque foi eleito deputado estadual .

No Podemos, a tendência é que a vaga de Ana Carolina Oliveira seja ocupada por Luiz Proteção Animal, já exerceu mandatos temporários como vereador suplente.

A cadeira de Sargento Nantes, do PP, deve ser herdada por Janaína Lima, ex-vereadora que não conseguiu retornar à Câmara na eleição municipal.

No PT, a eleição de Luna Zarattini abre caminho para o retorno de Manuel Del Rio, militante histórico do partido que também já foi vereador em São Paulo.

A saída de Thammy Miranda (PSD) para a Alesp deve beneficiar Aurélio Nomura, político experiente que já presidiu a Câmara Municipal e ficou na suplência da legenda nas eleições de 2024.

No MDB, o cenário é mais complexo. Desde agosto, a cadeira de Sidney Cruz, licenciado para atuar na prefeitura, é ocupada por Nunes Peixoto. O primeiro suplente da legenda, Paulo Frange, integra a equipe do prefeito Ricardo Nunes. Caso permaneça no Executivo, a tendência é que Nunes Peixoto continue exercendo o mandato na Câmara Municipal.

Já as saídas de Keit Lima e Marina Bragante devem beneficiar suplentes vinculados à federação PSOL-Rede – embora seja filiada ao PSB atualmente, Bragante foi eleita pela Rede em 2024.. A primeira vaga tende a ser ocupada por Débora Lima, liderança ligada às pautas de moradia e periferia. A segunda pode abrir espaço para Carol Iara, ativista de direitos humanos e que já foi co-vereadora da Bancada Feminista.

articles.title: Mãe de Isabella Nardoni, Ana Carolina Oliveira é eleita deputada federal por SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Ela teve 246.741 votos na disputa deste ano e chega à Câmara dos Deputados após dois anos de mandato como vereadora em São Paulo.
articles.summary: Ela teve 246.741 votos na disputa deste ano e chega à Câmara dos Deputados após dois anos de mandato como vereadora em São Paulo.
articles.body:
Ana Carolina Oliveira — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Ana Carolina Oliveira , mãe de Isabella Nardoni, foi eleita deputada federal por São Paulo nas eleições de 2026. Ela recebeu 246.741 votos, o equivalente a 1,04% dos votos válidos no estado, e foi a segunda candidata mais votada do Podemos no estado, atrás apenas do Delegado Palumbo, que teve 303.271 votos.

Aos 42 anos de idade, Ana Carolina amplia para o Congresso Nacional uma trajetória política iniciada há dois anos. Em 2024, ela foi eleita vereadora de São Paulo com 129.563 votos , ficando em segundo lugar entre os candidatos mais votados da cidade e sendo a mulher mais votada naquela eleição.

Na Câmara Municipal, sua atuação teve como principal bandeira a defesa de crianças e adolescentes e o combate à violência. Em 2025, foi eleita presidente da Comissão Extraordinária de Defesa dos Direitos da Criança, do Adolescente e da Juventude. Em 2026, foi reeleita para comandar o colegiado.

Agora, Ana Carolina deixará a Câmara Municipal para assumir uma cadeira na Câmara dos Deputados a partir de 2027.

Ana Carolina Oliveira mostra os porta-retratos com fotos de Isabella — Foto: Sérgio Fernandes/G1

Ana Carolina Cunha de Oliveira Francomano nasceu em São Paulo em 5 de abril de 1984. Antes de entrar para a política, construiu carreira no mercado financeiro. Segundo o perfil publicado pela Câmara Municipal, trabalhou durante 16 anos em uma instituição financeira privada e é formada em administração de empresas, com pós-graduação pela Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV).

Ela ficou conhecida nacionalmente em 2008, quando sua filha, Isabella Nardoni, então com 5 anos, morreu após ser jogada da janela do 6º andar de um prédio na Zona Norte de São Paulo.

O crime ocorreu em 29 de março daquele ano. O pai da menina, Alexandre Nardoni, e a madrasta, Anna Carolina Jatobá, foram condenados pela morte de Isabella em 2010.

A partir da morte da filha, Ana Carolina passou a falar publicamente sobre o caso e sobre a violência contra crianças. Anos depois, essa experiência se tornou também uma das bases de sua entrada na política.

Anna Carolina Jatobá, Isabella Nardoni e Alexandre Nardoni — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo/TV Globo

Em março de 2026, quando a morte de Isabella completou 18 anos, Ana Carolina fez uma nova homenagem à filha.

A data, que desde 2008 faz parte da história pública de Ana Carolina, ocorreu no mesmo ano em que ela disputou uma vaga na Câmara dos Deputados.

Durante a campanha eleitoral, a defesa de crianças e adolescentes e o combate à violência continuaram entre as principais bandeiras apresentadas por ela.

articles.title: Roraima garante a Flávio Bolsonaro maior votação percentual do Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Flávio Bolsonaro, do PL, venceu em 14 dos 15 municípios roraimenses. Lula venceu apenas em Uiramutã, no Norte do estado. Os dois vão disputar a presidência no Brasil em 25 de outubro.
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro, do PL, venceu em 14 dos 15 municípios roraimenses. Lula venceu apenas em Uiramutã, no Norte do estado. Os dois vão disputar a presidência em 25 de outubro.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro em agenda de camapanha nas eleições 2026 em Boa Vista, Roraima. — Foto: Nalu Cardoso/g1 RR

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) foi o candidato à Presidência do Brasil mais votado pela população roraimense no primeiro turno das eleições, neste domingo (4). Ele recebeu 71,06% dos votos válidos , o maior percentual entre os estados brasileiros . Veja como foi a apuração .

Flávio Bolsonaro obteve 231.322 votos no estado. Foram 156.902 votos a mais do que o obtido pelo candidato Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que teve 74.420 votos no estado (22,86%).

Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula vão disputar o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais , em 25 de outubro. Eles deixaram para trás outros dez candidatos .

No estado, os eleitores elegeram ex-prefeito de Boa Vista Arthur Henrique , também do PL, como governador neste domingo. Ele recebeu 220.809 votos , mais que o dobro da votação do principal adversário, o governador interino Soldado Sampaio (Republicanos).

Votação para presidente em Roraima — Foto: Arte/g1

Flávio Bolsonaro venceu em 14 dos 15 municípios de Roraima . O único em que perdeu para Lula foi Uiramutã , no Norte do Brasil e a cidade proporcionalmente mais indígena do país. Lá, o petista recebeu 68,95 % dos votos, o equivalente a 5.375 votos, e Flávio teve 2.327 (29,85%).

Entre os municípios de Roraima, Flávio teve o maior percentual de votos em Mucajaí , com 78,56%. Depois aparecem Caroebe , com 77,07%, e a capital Boa Vista , com 73,38%. Os dois primeiros municípios ficam no Sul do estado.

Em Roraima e no Brasil, Flávio r ecebeu mais votos no primeiro turno de 2026 do que o pai , Jair Bolsonaro, na mesma etapa das eleições de 2018 e 2022.

Jair foi eleito presidente em 2018 e perdeu a disputa pela reeleição no segundo turno de 2022. Na última eleição, Jair Bolsonaro recebeu 207.587 votos em Roraima. Em 2018, foram 174.306 votos no estado.

No primeiro turno de 2022, Jair Bolsonaro recebeu 51.072.345 votos (43,2%) em todo o país e ficou atrás de Lula, que somou 57.259.504 votos (48,43%). Depois, foi derrotado no 2º turno.

Em 2018, Bolsonaro terminou o primeiro turno à frente de Fernando Haddad (PT), com 49.277.010 votos (46,03%), contra 31.342.051 (29,28%) do petista.

articles.title: Nepal encerra operações de busca e resgate após avalanche | G1
articles.standfirst: Autoridades do país estimam que precisam de quase US$ 5 bilhões para a recuperação inicial da infraestrutura destruída e apoio às milhares de pessoas deslocadas.
articles.summary: Autoridades do país estimam que precisam de quase US$ 5 bilhões para a recuperação inicial da infraestrutura destruída e apoio às milhares de pessoas deslocadas.
articles.body:
O Nepal encerrou, nesta segunda-feira (5), a operação de busca e resgate das pessoas que ainda estão desaparecidas após a devastadora avalanche de lama que atingiu a fronteira do país com o Tibete, na China, em agosto , informaram autoridades.

Segundo o chefe do Centro Nacional de Operações de Emergência nepalense, Phanindra Paudel, o governo está avaliando como declarar legalmente as pessoas desaparecidas como falecidas, para permitir que suas famílias ou parentes concluam trâmites relacionados a seguros, bancos e outras formalidades legais.

Pelo menos 5.285 pessoas não foram encontradas após a tragédia que teve 1.455 mortes confirmadas até o momento.

“Estamos passando da fase de busca e resgate para a fase de reabilitação. Estamos iniciando os trâmites legais necessários para concluir as formalidades exigidas”, afirmou Paudel.

Equipes de resgate participando de uma operação de salvamento perto do túnel do Projeto Hidrelétrico Trishuli 3A, no Nepal — Foto: Nepal Prime Minister's Office via Reuters

Dharam Raj Uprety, chefe da Autoridade Nacional de Redução e Gestão de Riscos de Desastres, disse que as autoridades não irão mais procurar ativamente por corpos, mas recuperarão quaisquer restos mortais, bens ou outros objetos de valor encontrados durante o processo de reabilitação.

A enchente também destruiu 12 projetos hidrelétricos , estradas, pontes, fazendas e assentamentos.

As autoridades estimam que precisam de quase US$5 bilhões para a recuperação inicial dessa infraestrutura e apoio das milhares de pessoas deslocadas.

articles.title: France closes up to 500 schools Monday over student protests
articles.summary: Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some high schools after clashes between riot police and student protesters, France's education minister says...
articles.body:
Up to 500 schools across France will be partially or totally closed on Monday after clashes between riot police and student protesters in recent days, the French education minister said on Sunday.

Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some "400 to 500" high schools as security conditions "have not been fulfilled", Édouard Geffray said.

He also said 24 schools had been "burned or ransacked" since the start of the protests.

Thousands of students have been demonstrating over education standards and the protests, which started last week, have spread from Paris to other cities, including Montpellier, Nantes and Marseille.

High school pupils and others have objected to a lack of teachers, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings.

On Friday, French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said 735 of France's 3,700 schools had been affected "one way or another" by violent protests.

The education minister warned the number of schools potentially affected on Monday could be comparable to Friday's figure but promised a "partial, progressive return to lessons".

"There are activists - particularly from the far-left - who have infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves, and engaged in extreme violence," Édouard Geffray claimed.

"Clearly, this poses a risk to both our staff and our students," he said. Geffray added that 78 staff members in education had been wounded, which he described as "something we have never seen before".

On Friday 1,747 people were arrested, according to French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.

Over 5,000 people have been arrested altogether since the start of the movement, according the AFP news agency, with around 85% of them minors.

Organisers of the protests have called for the demonstrations to continue on Tuesday after accusing the government of a lack of "concrete measures", according to AFP.

On Sunday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said his government is taking further steps to "address the difficulties faced by high school students and educational staff".

He said this includes ensuring classes continue, improving facilities, better organising school days and making the French university admissions platform more transparent.

Lecornu also said the government is accelerating the review of its "vandal-pays" bill to ensure that people responsible for damage bear the cost of their actions.

articles.title: Christa Pike’s lawyers had warned execution would be ‘difficult and perhaps cruel’ due to her veins
articles.summary: Ex-lawyer for woman Tennessee attempted to execute says defense filings said she was at risk for ‘exactly what happened’
articles.body:
A former lawyer for Christa Pike says he was not surprised that Tennessee botched its attempt to execute her because attorneys had warned that problems accessing her veins could make the procedure dangerous and potentially cruel.

James Crowson, who represented Pike during part of her post-conviction appeals, said he had followed the case from afar before the failed execution at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville on 30 September.

"Well, I can't say I'm surprised," said Crowson, who represented Pike while working for the Tennessee Post-Conviction Defender. "I knew that there were a number of defense filings saying that she had compromised veins, and that was going to be a difficult and perhaps cruel procedure for her because it was going to put her at risk for exactly what happened."

Pike, 50, on Sunday remained hospitalized and on a machine helping her breathe after Tennessee administered two doses of pentobarbital that failed to kill her, as far as an attorney now representing her knew, the lawyer said on the CNN program State of the Union.

"She's still in the hospital, on a ventilator, critically ill – we don't really know the prognosis yet and may not know for several days," Stephen Ferrell, an assistant federal defender, said to CNN host Jake Tapper.

Ferrell told Tapper that he had not been able to personally see Pike, but "this is the extent of what we know".

Pike's attorneys allege improperly placed intravenous lines allowed the drug with which she was injected to enter tissue rather than her bloodstream, leaving both arms severely injured.

The Tennessee Department of Correction has maintained that it followed every step of the state's lawful execution protocol. And the department said the protocol did not permit additional procedures after the steps carried out on Wednesday.

Crowson said the accounts that officials followed the written protocol and that the execution was badly mishandled are not necessarily contradictory.

"The state comes up with a protocol and, typically, states that are inclined to impose the death penalty don't really include medicine or science in the discussions when they're coming up with these protocols," he said.

Crowson said the reported injuries appeared consistent with the concerns raised before the execution, citing the theory that the drug entered surrounding tissue instead of circulating properly through Pike's bloodstream.

Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 torture and killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow student at the Knoxville Job Corps. Pike was 18 at the time. Her then boyfriend and co-defendant, Tadaryl Shipp, was 17 and was ineligible for the death penalty. He received a sentence of life imprisonment.

That gap in punishment based on a small age difference remains significant to Crowson. He said it illustrates what he views as the capricious nature of capital punishment.

"She's a few months older than the young man that was engaged in the same conduct, and she's been fighting for her life now for 32 years," Crowson said. "He's still in prison, but hasn't been subjected to the death penalty."

He said the age of 18 that was decisive for Pike "just seems like an arbitrary number".

Crowson represented Pike during a stage of her post-conviction case about 16 years earlier and said he visited her "dozens of times" on death row. He said he last spoke with her in 2009.

He described Pike at the time as "very superficially charming" and attentive to people around her. But he said the person he knew bore little resemblance to the teenager whose crime sent her to death row.

"I never saw the Christa that committed those crimes that put her in prison," Crowson said. "That person exists, obviously."

The core of the post-conviction appeal, he said, was ineffective assistance of counsel. His team argued that Pike's original attorneys failed to adequately present evidence about her mental illness, brain damage and history of severe childhood abuse during the sentencing phase.

Pike ultimately exhausted her appeals without ever getting relief, despite her attorneys' offering evidence of being diagnosed with bipolar and post-traumatic stress disorders.

"It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I'd done," Pike had said in an earlier petition for clemency. "Even more to accept how many lives I affected. I took the life of someone's child, sister, friend. It sickens me now to think I had the ability to commit such a crime."

Crowson more recently said "there was a lot that was left out" at the time of Pike's conviction.

"Would it have made a difference? I don't know. There are a lot of people who feel very strongly, and her crime was grisly and horrifying."

What happens next depends on whether Pike ultimately survives the botched execution – and, if she does, the extent of any lasting injuries.

Crowson said he expects intense pressure on Bill Lee, Tennessee's governor, to commute Pike's sentence to life imprisonment if she recovers. If she suffered serious neurological damage, he said, questions about her competency would become central to any attempt by Tennessee to execute her again.

The fallout of the botched execution widened on Saturday when Lee announced that Frank Strada, the Tennessee Department of Correction commissioner, would resign later in October. Lee has ordered an independent review and halted executions in the state for the remainder of the year.

Strada's resignation was a predictable consequence of a botched execution now under national scrutiny, according to Crowson, who said: "Whenever you have a disaster like this, there's going to be some fallout."

Furthermore, Pike's was at least the fifth execution Strada had botched since 2022 in Tennessee as well as Arizona, where he previously worked, according to death penalty lawyers.

Crowson said he hopes that Pike's case results in the government taking a closer look at the death penalty as a functional legal punishment. He said there is a clear pattern between people who are sentenced to death and their history of trauma and mental illness not being accounted for during trial and sentencing.

"I think we as a nation have a strange relationship with mental illness," he said. "It's just so often discounted and mocked. It's unfortunate."

images.caption: Christa Pike in court in Nashville in 2012. Photograph: Dipti Vaidya/USA TODAY NETWORK/Imagn Images/Reuters Connect

articles.title: Chirag Paswan's UP gamble: Why PM Modi's 'Hanuman' is flexing his muscle against allies
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Chirag Paswan once described himself as Prime Minister Narendra Modi's \"Hanuman\".
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chirag Paswan once described himself as Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "Hanuman". Six years later, the LJP (Ram Vilas) chief offered another approach of his politics: "I can stand up to my government ... I am in the alliance but I am not the BJP."This distinction becomes relevant as he prepares to take his party into the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election. LJP(RV) has announced that it will contest the polls and is preparing for all 403 constituencies, while leaving open whether it will eventually contest alone or as part of an alliance.We want this to take the form of a legal right for the youth. Wherever exams are cancelled, students should receive reimbursement for their travel expenses, arrangements for their accommodation, and provisions for their food. We have firmly presented this stance of the party on the floor of the House as well.The UP move comes after a significant change in Chirag Paswan's political position. In 2020, the undivided LJP broke with the NDA in Bihar, contested 135 seats and targeted Nitish Kumar's JD(U), while maintaining its support for PM Modi. Its slogan captured the strategy: "Modi se bair nahi, Nitish teri khair nahi." The party won only one seat, but its 5.66% vote share had a measurable impact on the results.Since then, LJP(RV) has moved from being a marginal alliance partner to a more consequential NDA component. It won all five Lok Sabha seats it contested in Bihar in 2024, giving Chirag Paswan a 100% strike rate, and in the 2025 assembly election it contested 29 seats under the NDA arrangement and won 19. The BJP and JD(U) contested 101 seats each, while LJP(RV) secured 29.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();That progression provides the context for the 403-seat announcement. Chirag Paswan now has five Lok Sabha MPs, 19 MLAs in Bihar and a Union cabinet position. The question is whether that political weight can be extended beyond Bihar.The 403-seat gambleThe latest phase of the UP push took shape in September, when Paswan launched his party's youth outreach in Prayagraj. At the "Youth Bole Toh" programme, he spoke about education, employment, skills and greater youth participation in politics, and announced plans for a National Youth Commission.On September 28, he made the electoral plan explicit: "There is no doubt that LJP (Ram Vilas) will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections."The following day, he said the response in Prayagraj had strengthened his confidence in the UP plan. LJP(RV) MP Rajesh Verma subsequently said the party was preparing for all 403 seats, while making clear that the eventual alliance arrangement would be decided later.The 2020 flashbackThe 2020 Bihar assembly election was the debut test of Chirag Paswan's leadership. His father, Ram Vilas Paswan, had just died a few days ago.The LJP won only one seat but emerged as a significant factor in 54 constituencies where its vote total was greater than the victory margin. In 25 seats where JD(U) finished second, LJP's vote exceeded the winning margin. Chirag was explicit about the objective, saying after the election: "My main idea in the election was to make the BJP stronger. I am happy with the impact I have had in this election."The BJP finished with 74 seats in that election, ahead of JD(U)'s 43 for the first time. The episode demonstrated that LJP did not need to win seats itself to affect the relative strength of its larger alliance partner.The 2025 Bihar election showed the other side of the equation. LJP(RV) was no longer operating as a spoiler outside the alliance. It contested 29 seats as an NDA partner and won 19, converting its electoral relevance into representation inside the alliance.UP could now test both models: LJP(RV) as an alliance partner with an electoral base of its own, and LJP(RV) as a potential vote-splitter in constituencies where even a few thousand votes can decide the outcome.The Dalit arithmeticThe potential constituency is significant, but far from straightforward.The BSP won no seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha election in UP and polled around 9.4%. At the same time, the SP expanded its support among Dalit voters as part of its broader PDA coalition. A Lokniti-CSDS post-poll analysis showed a sharp difference between Jatav and non-Jatav Dalit voting patterns, with the BSP retaining much stronger support among Jatavs than among non-Jatav Dalits.For Chirag Paswan, the challenge is therefore larger than taking the Paswan identity from Bihar to UP. Pasis, Valmikis, Khatiks and other non-Jatav communities have distinct political histories and local calculations. Whether LJP(RV) can persuade sections of these voters that it is a credible political vehicle will determine whether its UP expansion produces votes or merely an organisational footprint.The impact could also vary by constituency. A modest LJP(RV) vote could matter in a close BJP-SP contest if it draws disproportionately from one side's potential support base. But unlike Bihar in 2020, there is no single obvious target. The BJP, SP, BSP and Congress have overlapping social coalitions, making the direction of any vote transfer harder to predict.Why UP and why now?The UP expansion also fits Paswan's attempt to establish LJP(RV) beyond its Bihar base. The party has already demonstrated that it can operate outside the state: in the 2023 Nagaland assembly election, it contested 16 seats, won two and finished runner-up in eight, securing more than 8.6% of the vote.But UP is on a different scale. A credible organisation here would give Chiag Paswan a political presence in the country's largest state and potentially strengthen his position in future NDA negotiations.His recent conduct suggests that maintaining an independent identity is part of that calculation. He has criticised the Bihar government's handling of law and order while remaining part of the NDA, and questioned the Election Commission over concerns surrounding SIR before welcoming its subsequent clarification.The UP experiment, therefore, would not simply be about how many seats LJP(RV) could win. It would be abot whether Chirag Paswan can build an influence outside Bihar to make his party a more consequential NDA partner, while retaining the political independence he summed up in his own words: "I am in the alliance but I am not the BJP."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Workers clearing land for a solar farm in New Hampshire cut 30 trees on the wrong property; settlement with the electric company and tree service hit $100,000
articles.summary: A routine land-clearing project in Rockingham County, New Hampshire, turned into a costly property dispute after workers hired to prepare land for a solar
articles.body: A routine land-clearing project in Rockingham County, New Hampshire, turned into a costly property dispute after workers hired to prepare land for a solar farm mistakenly cut more than 30 trees belonging to a neighbouring landowner. The property boundaries had reportedly been surveyed and marked before the work began, but the tree-service workers apparently misunderstood which trees they were supposed to remove. The trees, some with trunks up to 26 inches in diameter, had also served as a visual buffer between the homeowner's property and the solar farm. After an insurance demand failed, the landowner sued the tree service and the electric company. Following months of litigation and mediation in early 2026, the case ended with a $100,000 settlement.Workers cut trees on wrong propertyThe incident occurred in 2024, when an electric company hired a tree service to clear land for a solar farm in Rockingham County. According to the law firm representing the affected landowner, the property boundaries had already been surveyed and marked before the clearing work began. Despite this, workers apparently misunderstood which trees they had been instructed to remove and crossed onto neighbouring land. More than 30 trees belonging to another property owner were cut during the operation, according to the firm's account.Trees had provided a visual bufferThe trees were not merely timber standing on unused land. The law firm's case summary says they provided a partial visual buffer between the affected property and the solar farm. The stumps reportedly measured between 7 and 26 inches in diameter, indicating that some of the trees were substantial. Their removal changed the view from the property and reduced the natural screening between the homeowner's land and the solar installation. The case therefore involved not only the cutting of trees but also their importance to the property's appearance and surroundings.Insurance claim led to lawsuitAfter discovering that the trees had been removed, the property owner hired Welts, White & Fontaine, PC, with attorney Israel F. Piedra handling the matter. The law firm said it submitted a demand to the tree service's insurance company, but no settlement offer was received. The dispute subsequently moved into litigation. articles.title: In 2016, another Iowa corn-and-soy farmer collected about $20,000 a year from turbines, giving his farm a cash floor when crop prices were below costs
articles.summary: Discover how Iowa corn and soybean farmers are augmenting their earnings with wind turbine leases, providing a steady income source amidst fluctuating crop prices. Learn about the broader impact of wind power on rural economies in the Midwest.
articles.body: For farmers whose earnings depend heavily on the price of corn and soybeans, a poor harvest is not the only financial risk. Even when crops perform well, falling commodity prices can leave little room between the cost of production and what the harvest brings in. In 2016, an Iowa farmer found another source of income on his farmland: wind turbines.According to the Omaha World-Herald, Tim Hemphill, a corn and soybean farmer outside Milford, Iowa, was receiving about $20,000 a year from leasing land for wind turbines. The figure was reported in 2016 and later repeated by the Advanced Power Alliance. The arrangement reflected a wider change taking place across Iowa, where wind power had become an important part of the state's electricity supply while providing some rural landowners with an additional source of income.When crop prices fellThe timing of Hemphill's wind income was important. In 2016, Iowa's farmers had to face a period characterised by low commodity prices. The Omaha World-Herald stated that the cost of growing corn might be quite high compared to the market price, which would put some pressure on the farmers who mainly relied on their crops to earn an income. Hemphill said corn had once sold for about $7 a bushel, while his production costs were about $4.20 a bushel.Against that backdrop, a wind lease worked differently from a crop sale. The farmer did not have to harvest an additional crop from the land occupied by the turbine. Instead, the energy company paid for the right to use the site for wind-energy infrastructure. The amount a farmer receives depends on the contract and the number and capacity of turbines involved. A US Government Accountability Office review found that wind-farm lease payments varied considerably between projects and could reach tens of thousands of dollars a year for individual farmers. For Hemphill, the reported $20,000 annual payment therefore represented a relatively predictable addition to farm income at a time when crop revenue was much less certain.Farming beneath the turbinesThe presence of wind turbines did not automatically translate to the surrounding agricultural lands becoming useless to the farmer. The land taken up by the turbine foundation, roads and other infrastructure is minimal, and farming can continue on the surrounding land. A 2021 report on Iowa farmer Kelly Nieuwenhuis offers an example: he had two MidAmerican Energy turbines on his farm, while the surrounding land was still used for corn and soybean farming. The turbines’ infrastructure covered about two acres, and the landowner also received lease income.Research has also examined what happens to farmland values when turbines are installed. A study in the Journal of Agricultural and Resource Economics found that lease payments were one factor that could affect the value of farmland hosting turbines, along with roads, turbine pads and possible disruption to farming operations. Lease terms, infrastructure requirements, access and the amount of land taken out of production all formed part of the economic calculation.A different kind of farm revenueWind development was important not only for electricity production in Iowa. Indeed, in 2015, Iowa generated 31% of its electricity from wind, the largest share among U.S. states. That year, Iowa farmers received millions of dollars in wind-lease payments. According to a 2024 report on farm operations, 3.5 per cent of farms received energy payments related to wind, oil or natural gas, and those payments averaged more than $30,000 a year in 2020.For a farmer like Hemphill, the benefit was even more direct. His profit from corn and soybeans might fluctuate with market forces, but his wind lease was guaranteed. The turbines were not a replacement for farming, but another business activity on the same agricultural land. The 2016 story reflected a broader trend across parts of the American Midwest: land could generate value not only from crops, but also from wind leases.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 1970, Fullerton paved a 600-foot California street with crushed waste glass; 2 years later, the EPA found the unusual recycled road was still in good condition
articles.summary: Discover how Fullerton, California pioneered the use of crushed waste glass in asphalt in 1970, paving a 600-foot road that impressively stood the test of time. Learn about the innovative experiments that transformed bottles into durable road materials and the ongoing implications for recycling and infrastructure.
articles.body: In 1970, a street in Fullerton, California, became an unusual experiment in recycling when crushed waste glass was used as a major part of its asphalt surface. Instead of sending unwanted bottles to disposal, the material was processed and incorporated into a road mixture that covered part of a 600-foot stretch in the Fullerton Air Industrial Park. At the time, researchers were investigating whether discarded bottles could replace some or all of the conventional mineral aggregate used in asphalt. The Fullerton experiment provided an opportunity to observe how such a material behaved under actual traffic rather than only in laboratory tests.Turning bottles into road materialAccording to the EPA report, the Fullerton street was paved on October 26, 1970. The road was 600 feet long and 40 feet wide, although only 30 feet of its width received the glass-containing asphalt. The remaining 10 feet was paved with conventional asphaltic concrete, providing a comparison within the same road. The glass came from clean, non-returnable bottles collected at a Fullerton bottle redemption centre and crushed in a hammermill. The resulting glass aggregate was then blended with rock dust and hydrated lime.The final aggregate mix consisted of 63% glass, 36% rock dust, and 1% hydrated lime. Then, a 3-inch-thick layer was laid over a crushed rock base of 7.5 inches. The inclusion of hydrated lime in the aggregate was intentional. It had been previously discovered in laboratory testing that lime addition would enhance the water-resistance properties of glass-asphalt mixtures. The EPA study found that asphalt mixes could be produced with crushed glass aggregates and conventional paving equipment, though compaction was challenging.What happened after the road opened?The initial construction process revealed one of the practical problems associated with using glass in asphalt. Because it tended to flow under pressure at high temperatures, the Fullerton mix was rolled only after it cooled to 220°F or lower. Core samples showed an average compaction density of 93.5%, and no further density changes were noted the following year.Another test was done on the skid resistance of the road by the California Division of Highways in March 1971. The test found skid numbers of 61 to 69 at 25 miles per hour, equivalent to 54 to 62 at 40 miles per hour. After a year, the surface showed some ravelling caused by fractures in the larger glass particles. Even so, the surface was still rated good, and the pavement performance was considered satisfactory. Later analysis provided additional evidence about aggregate performance. There were no signs of excessive degradation of the aggregate on the Fullerton and Rolla roads, according to the EPA report. In Fullerton, the aggregate gradation change was minimal.An early experiment in glassphaltHowever, the use of glass-in-asphalt in Fullerton was not an isolated case. At about the same time, similar trials were carried out in Missouri, Ontario, Pennsylvania, and other regions. As stated by the EPA summary for 1975, the field installations usually provided adequate skid resistance and satisfactory performance from a structural point of view; however, surface ravelling was observed in some cases. In a subsequent report issued by the Federal Highway Administration, the Fullerton trial installation was described as 600 feet long and made of asphalt material with 63 per cent of crushed glass in the aggregate composition. This does not mean the experiment proved waste glass was always a better alternative to traditional road aggregates. Rather, the experiment showed that used bottles could be converted into asphalt material and tested under real traffic conditions.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Taylor Sheridan bought a 600-acre Texas ranch in 2013 as a family home; years later, Bosque Ranch is a film and TV production base, equine competition hub and concert venue with more than 150 horses
articles.summary: Explore how Taylor Sheridan transformed his 600-acre Texas ranch into a bustling production site for television and film, alongside hosting equine competitions and live entertainment.
articles.body: American filmmaker, screenwriter, and actor Taylor Sheridan bought a 600-acre ranch in Weatherford, Texas, in 2013 as a family home. More than a decade later, the property has become a production location for his television projects.Known as Bosque Ranch, the property is about 40 miles from Fort Worth and serves as the headquarters of Bosque Ranch Productions, the company behind shows including Yellowstone, 1883, 1923, Landman, Lawmen: Bass Reeves, Tulsa King and Mayor of Kingstown.The ranch has also become closely tied to Sheridan's interest in Western sports. It hosts cutting and reining competitions, including the annual NCHA Brazos Bash, and serves as the training centre of Kelby Phillips, the 2018 NRCHA World's Greatest Horseman rider.From family home to filming locationSheridan grew up in Texas and had planned to return to the state with his wife, actress Nicole Muirbrook, and their son, Gus.Speaking on the Rodeo Time podcast earlier this year, Sheridan said he had expected to step away from television after Yellowstone.“I was set up to retire. I was going to be done after Yellowstone. I’d bought the ranch in Weatherford, [Texas], and I paid cash. I didn’t owe anybody anything,” he said.He planned to spend more time riding horses and maintaining what he described as a “little hobby herd”.That did not happen.Sheridan continued expanding his television work, and the ranch itself became part of that business. In 2021, he began filming 1883, the Yellowstone prequel, at the property.The location reportedly became another revenue stream, with Paramount paying $50,000 a week to use the ranch for production, plus an additional $25 per cow, as per Elle Decor magazine.The property remains the family's primary residence, although details of the home itself have not been made public.A ranch built around horsesThe entertainment business is only one part of Bosque Ranch.The 600-acre property operates as an equine facility, with facilities for professional horse competitions and training. More than 150 horses are associated with the ranch.Its events include cutting and reining competitions, sports that fit closely with Sheridan's interest in Western culture and horsemanship.The ranch is also home to the annual NCHA Brazos Bash and serves as the training centre for Phillips, who won the 2018 NRCHA World's Greatest Horseman competition.Sheridan's expanding Texas footprintBosque Ranch is also part of a much larger collection of ranch properties Sheridan has acquired in recent years.His biggest purchase came in 2022, when he led a group that acquired the 266,000-acre Four Sixes Ranch in Texas for $330 million.Sheridan had previously said he intended to retire after Yellowstone. He signed major deals with Paramount and later agreed to a deal with NBCUniversal that could be worth as much as $1 billion, according to the magazine.Production baseSheridan bought the Weatherford property as a family home in 2013. It has since taken on a much larger role in his career.Today, the 600-acre Bosque Ranch serves as both a residence and a hub for TV production, equestrian events and live shows.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bypolls in 5 assembly constituencies, 1 Lok Sabha seat tomorrow: Key contests to watch
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission (EC) will conduct byelections on Tuesday for five assembly seats and one Lok Sabha constituency across three states and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission (EC) will conduct byelections on Tuesday for five assembly seats and one Lok Sabha constituency across three states and the Union territory of Puducherry, with vote counting scheduled for Friday.The constituencies going to the polls are Madurantakam and Dharapuram in Tamil Nadu, Thattanchavady in Puducherry, Rejinagar and Nandigram in West Bengal, and Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency in Assam.The bypolls come amid growing scrutiny of the Election Commission (EC) over reported differences between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. The Indian Express reported last month that Sandhu and Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge.The report triggered protests seeking Kumar’s resignation, even as the EC maintained that all decisions had been taken unanimously by the CEC and the Election Commissioners. The issue has also reached the Supreme Court, which took up a petition seeking Kumar's removal, and issued notices to the EC and the Centre.However, the Chief Justice Surya Kant-led bench declined to pass an interim order, observing that it could not do so based solely on a media report whose accuracy remained uncertain.Will Vijay’s ‘magic’ charm Tamil Nadu againThe bypolls in Madurantakam and Dharapuram will be the first major electoral test for chief minister C Joseph Vijay since his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) came to power following the April assembly elections, just two years after the party was launched. A total of 27 candidates are contesting in Madurantakam, while 30 are in the fray in Dharapuram.The vacancies arose after AIADMK MLAs Maragatham Kumaravel of Madurantakam and P Sathyabama of Dharapuram resigned from their seats. Both subsequently joined TVK and have been fielded by the party in the bypolls.The DMK, led by former chief minister MK Stalin, as well as the AIADMK and CPI, have also fielded candidates. The CPI is among the parties that supported TVK after it emerged as the single-largest party, paving the way for it to form the government.Suvendu Adhikari on test in West BengalIn West Bengal, the focus is on Nandigram, which fell vacant after Suvendu Adhikari, now the BJP’s first chief minister in the state, resigned as its MLA. Adhikari defeated Mamata Banerjee in Bhabanipur and retained his Nandigram stronghold in the April assembly elections. He chose to represent Bhabanipur, vacating Nandigram and necessitating the bypoll. The BJP has fielded Hasirani Rath, whose son Chandranath, an aide of Adhikari, was shot dead days after the assembly election results were announced.The TMC, which was voted out after 15 years and has since split into two factions, decided not to field a candidate after its original nominee, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew from the contest. It instead extended support to the Congress. However, in a twist, Congress candidate Milan Pradhan was arrested hours later in connection with a 2007 case. On September 29, the Calcutta high court granted him interim bail till October 21, while the Supreme Court adjourned the West Bengal government’s plea challenging the order, paving the way for Pradhan to contest the bypoll.The rival TMC faction is also in the fray, having nominated Mohammad Eteshamul Haque, while the CPI has fielded Santigopal Giri.The other seat, Rejinagar, fell vacant after Humayun Kabir resigned as MLA. Kabir had earlier formed his own Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) after being suspended and subsequently expelled by the TMC. He also won the Nowda seat and chose to represent it, prompting him to field his son, Golam Nabi Azad, from Rejinagar, where around 70% of voters belong to the minority community.The BJP has fielded Sakharav Sarkar, while the CPI(M) has nominated Syed Asad Ali. The Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction has fielded Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, while the rival faction has nominated Safiuzzaman Sheikh. The Congress candidate is Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi.BJP aims to wrest Nagaon from Congress in AssamIn Assam, the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll was necessitated by the resignation of then-Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi, who switched to the BJP in April ahead of the assembly elections, which the saffron party won, securing a third straight term. The contest is significant for the Congress, which held the seat after Bordoloi won it in 2019 and 2024. The party has fielded former MLA Sibamoni Bora, while the BJP has nominated Devasish Sharma.AIUDF president Badruddin Ajmal is also contesting after replacing the party’s original nominee, Rejaul Karim Sarkar. With more than 55% of Nagaon’s voters belonging to the minority community, the contest among the BJP, Congress and AIUDF is being closely watched, despite 15 candidates being in the fray.Thattanchavady: NDA's popularity test in PuducherryThe Thattanchavady bypoll is being seen as a test of the four-month-old NDA government led by chief minister N Rangasamy. The seat fell vacant after Rangasamy, who won both Thattanchavady and Mangalam in the April assembly elections, kept Mangalam.The All India NR Congress, which leads the NDA government, has fielded Ashok Anand, while the DMK and Congress have nominated K Sethu Selvam and E Vinayagam, respectively. The Congress has the backing of its Tamil Nadu ally TVK. Eleven candidates are in the fray.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday nominated Mehrdad Akhlaghi as his pick to head the defence ministry, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.Akhlaghi most recently held a senior executive post within the ministry itself, and earlier served as chief operating officer of the Aerospace Industries Organisation.The Iranian Parliament is expected to review Akhlaghi’s proposed plans in the relevant committee before holding a confidence vote.The ministry has had no permanent leader since the beginning of the US-Iran war, when brigadier general Aziz Nasirzadeh was killed during the initial airstrikes. Since then, a number of military commanders have led the ministry on a temporary basis.Yemen launches major operation against HouthisOn the ground in Yemen, the army of the internationally recognised government says it has retaken the Dhubab district along with key positions close to Bab al-Mandeb. The announcement came one day after the army said it had begun a major offensive named "Yemen Dawn" against the Houthis.The Houthis, however, have denied the claim. Al Jazeera reported.Yemen's pro-government Saba news agency, citing a military source, also reported that government forces have seized Mocha, a strategic port city west of Taiz province. In September, the Iran-aligned group had made major gains along Yemen's western Red Sea coast, capturing the strategic city and several Red Sea islands. These advances gave them control of Yemen's side of the Bab el-Mandeb, a narrow maritime passage linking the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.Mocha has remained a central prize in the fighting between Houthi forces and the Saudi-backed government.The city's location is the reason its fate matters well beyond Yemen. It lies roughly 75km north of the Bab al-Mandeb strait, the waterway linking the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.Separately, Iranian officials responded to the Houthi control over the Mandeb strait. Senior advisor to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, major-general Yahya Rahim Safavi, said the development was "another step in the larger defeat of the United States in the region".He argued that Washington had been unable to manage the Gulf's "security arrangements", even after pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into military bases and weapons there.You use AI every day.
