articles.title: Dibrugarh's river trade returns after 70 years: First post-Independence cargo from Assam heads to Bangladesh
articles.summary: Dibrugarh on Monday resumed international river trade after nearly seven decades, with Union Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal flagging off a barge
articles.body: Dibrugarh on Monday resumed international river trade after nearly seven decades, with Union Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal flagging off a barge carrying 540 metric tonnes of methanol from Bogibeel Terminal to Dhaka, marking the first cargo shipment from upper Assam to a foreign port since Independence.The methanol, produced by state-owned Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd (APCL) at Namrup, will travel around 768 km along National Waterway-2 on the Brahmaputra before reaching the India-Bangladesh border and continuing through the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route. The voyage from Bogibeel to Narayanganj in Bangladesh will cover around 1,300 km.The shipment is being seen as a test of the Brahmaputra's potential as a commercially viable freight corridor connecting the Northeast with overseas markets. Regular methanol shipments to Bangladesh are planned, with the movement enabled by recently established customs and immigration facilities at Bogibeel and Dhubri.The voyage also revives Dibrugarh's river trade nearly 70 years after its historic river ghat shut down. The ghat closed in 1956 as tea shipments shifted to rail, ending regular river bookings from the town.“Our grandparents grew up hearing the steamer whistle at Dibrugarh Ghat. For 70 years, that whistle fell silent and the ships stopped coming,” Sonowal said. “Today, a ship leaves Dibrugarh for the world once again. The river never failed us. What it lacked for decades was the will to revive it.”The vessel DLB Patkai, pushed by the tug Kushal Konwar, will carry the cargo to Pangaon Port in Dhaka. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma joined the flag-off ceremony virtually.Sarma described the shipment as a significant moment for the state, saying, “Assam's own product, made in Namrup, is now traveling to an international market on Assam's own river. The Northeast is no longer a frontier. It is India's gateway to the East.”The revival of Dibrugarh's river connectivity has been supported by the Bogibeel passenger and cargo terminal, which opened in February 2024, along with customs and immigration infrastructure and the Jalvahak cargo incentive programme.The route has seen growing activity in recent years. Tata Steel barges reached Pandu through Bangladesh in February 2022, while the river cruise vessel MV Ganga Vilas travelled from Varanasi to Dibrugarh through Bangladesh in 2023.The government is also seeking to expand inland waterways as an alternative freight network. Cargo movement on India's national waterways rose from 18 million metric tonnes in 2013-14 to 218 million metric tonnes in 2025-26, according to the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.More than Rs 6,800 crore is being invested in waterways across the Northeast, including the development of National Waterway-2, a ship repair facility at Pandu and last-mile connectivity to Pandu Port.Sonowal said the economic and environmental case for waterways was also significant. “Every ton we move on the river means less fuel burnt and fewer trucks on the highway,” he said.The government is working with Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan and Myanmar to develop regional waterway links, with the Dibrugarh-Dhaka shipment potentially opening another freight route for products from the Northeast to international markets.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Simon Andriesz, a former British banker and whistleblower who had raised questions over US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged links to convicted
articles.body: Simon Andriesz, a former British banker and whistleblower who had raised questions over US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged links to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, has died by suicide, according to reports.Andriesz, 57, was previously a managing director at Wall Street firm BGC Group, where Lutnick served as chief executive. His death was confirmed by Andy Agathangelou, founder of the Transparency Task Force, a campaign group that had hosted events involving Andriesz.“It is with great sadness that we share the news that Simon Andriesz, a valued member of our community, passed away last week,” Agathangelou said, as quoted by The Banker.Andriesz had previously spoken to the BBC about evidence he said he had uncovered concerning Lutnick’s relationship with Epstein. According to the report, he told the BBC that he had found an email chain from 2018 in which Lutnick and Epstein discussed the prospects of a start-up business in which they were both involved.The allegations were examined in a BBC File on 4 Investigates episode broadcast in July, titled “The Epstein Files: Lutnick, the Royals and the British Whistleblower.”Lutnick and EpsteinLutnick acknowledged in February that he had visited Epstein’s private island in 2012, saying he had stopped there for lunch while travelling by boat with his family. He told the Senate Appropriations Committee that his wife, four children and nannies were also present.“I did have lunch with him as I was on a boat going across on a family vacation. My wife was with me, as were my four children and nannies... We had lunch on the island. That is true. For an hour,” Lutnick said.Lutnick had previously faced questions over his past association with Epstein. He has condemned Epstein’s crimes and said: “I unequivocally condemn the conduct attributed to Jeffrey Epstein and everyone who participated in his illegal activities. The survivors of his crimes deserve our respect and support.”Andriesz's last post goes viralOn August 9, Andriesz posted his last X post, where he presented links to his works and interviews. "The personal consequences of whistleblowing, and the retaliation I say followed, have been devastating for my family and me," he wrote, adding that he would be sharing more of the evidence and the story behind what happened.How did Andriesz die?The circumstances leading to his death are unknown. He was living in Cornwall as of July and was confirmed dead last week, reports said.Fundraiser by friendJohn Robertson, a friend and representative of Andriesz, said he set up a GoFundMe link to help Andriesz's son. "Simon Andriesz was a devoted father, a much-loved friend and someone who showed extraordinary courage in standing up for what he believed was right. Following Simon’s tragic death, those of us who knew and cared about him want to make sure that something positive and lasting is created for the son he leaves behind. We have established this fundraiser to support his son’s education, welfare and future opportunities. Every penny raised through this fundraiser is for Simon’s son. None of the organisers will receive or personally benefit from any of the money raised," it said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pentagon stops using Anthropic's AI tools, months after declaring it a supply chain risk
articles.summary: The US defence ministry has stopped using Anthropic's AI tools, months after labelling the company a supply chain risk on national security grounds.
articles.body: The US defence ministry has stopped using Anthropic's AI tools, months after labelling the company a supply chain risk on national security grounds.A department official told the BBC that the Pentagon "has ceased the use of Anthropic products."Defence secretary Pete Hegseth designated Anthropic a supply chain risk in February and announced that the Pentagon would phase out its use by late August.However, several people familiar with the matter told the BBC that, as recently as last week, the department was still using Anthropic's Claude model for research, analysis and intelligence gathering, as well as in military operations against Iran.These sources, who include former US defence officials and contractors who have worked closely with the Pentagon on AI, said the tool was regarded as critical for sorting through vast quantities of information.Anthropic spokesman declined to comment on the Pentagon's statement. BBC reported.It is unclear why the department has ended its use of the tools now, and the full severing of ties has not been reported before.The US government and military had used Anthropic since 2024, and it was the first advanced AI company to have its tools deployed in government agencies handling classified work. Earlier this year, however, the Pentagon pressed the company to remove Claude's safety guardrails and grant the military unrestricted access to its AI tools. Anthropic refused, citing concerns about mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. In response, Hegseth designated it a "national security supply-chain risk," a legal measure typically reserved for companies that pose a threat to the US.Anthropic called the move "unprecedented and unlawful" and has sued the Trump administration to overturn the designation.While the case has proceeded through the courts, the Pentagon has signed contracts with other major tech companies, including Google and OpenAI. According to two people familiar with AI use in the department, OpenAI's tools have been adopted more widely in some military departments in recent months.You use AI every day. articles.title: Linton-on-Ouse residents fear village could become ‘ghost town’ over plans for 1,200 asylum seekers; homeowners consider selling properties at losses of up to 20% as homes remain empty in 700-strong North Yorkshire community
articles.summary: Residents of a North Yorkshire village fear their community could become a “ghost town” if controversial plans to accommodate up to 1,200 adult male
articles.body: Residents of a North Yorkshire village fear their community could become a “ghost town” if controversial plans to accommodate up to 1,200 adult male asylum seekers at a former RAF base go ahead.Dozens of residents in Linton-on-Ouse, near York, have reportedly considered selling their homes and moving elsewhere amid uncertainty over the proposed asylum accommodation centre. According to SWNS, some homeowners have already put their properties on the market and say they could face losses of up to 20 per cent.The village, which has around 700 residents, has been at the centre of a renewed debate over plans to use the former RAF Linton-on-Ouse site to house asylum seekers.Residents say properties are being left emptyNew images from the village show around 35 newly renovated former Ministry of Defence homes across two new-build estates currently standing vacant, according to SWNS.Other nearby estates owned by property developer Annington have also reportedly seen residents moving in and out following the announcement of the proposed asylum centre.The Linton-on-Ouse Action Group surveyed 404 residents and found that 60 per cent of renters questioned said they were “very likely” to leave if the plans proceed, according to data cited by SWNS.Alice Sizer, 44, who moved into a three-bedroom home at Linton Meadows with her husband and five-year-old daughter in 2023, said she would consider leaving if the plans are approved.Sizer claimed she could lose around £100,000 by selling her property, including approximately £50,000 she has invested in the home.“We have a strong connection to the area as my husband’s dad was in the RAF and he was posted at the base for a short while,” she said.“Our daughter goes to the same school Ian went to and she loves it.”Sizer said her concerns were about feeling secure rather than race or religion.“We are normal working families. This isn’t about race or religion, just wanting to feel secure in our own homes,” she said.Homeowner says plans accelerated decision to moveLuke Feather, 28, a tradesman whose house is currently on the market, said the proposed asylum accommodation was a factor in his decision to move.Feather said he and his partner moved to Linton-on-Ouse in 2022 after earlier plans to use the RAF site for asylum accommodation had been dropped.“We had just got engaged and were looking for somewhere to settle down, and we couldn’t argue with the prices,” he said.“But when the migrant plans came up, it was upsetting as we love the area but it accelerated our plans to move out.”Former RAF base could house 1,200 menThe former RAF Linton-on-Ouse site was earmarked by the government in June for asylum accommodation.If approved, the centre is expected to house around 1,200 single men aged between 18 and 65. Residents have raised concerns about the potential scale of the facility in a village of around 700 people.The Home Office has said the site would be secure and would operate for a minimum of three years.The proposal is not the first attempt to use the location for asylum accommodation. Plans announced in 2022 to house around 1,500 asylum seekers at the former RAF base were subsequently abandoned.‘Ghost town’ fears returnResidents have drawn comparisons with 2022, when the departure of RAF personnel contributed to concerns about the village becoming increasingly empty.Just across from Linton Meadows is Linton Place, where 20 four-bedroom detached homes are owned by Annington. According to the information provided, only four of the properties are currently rented.Annington has been renovating former RAF housing in the area as part of its Linton Collection, with properties advertised for between £1,325 and £1,850 a month.Residents say the availability of homes has remained a concern since the asylum plans were announced.One elderly resident, who did not want to be named, said she moved in July after the proposal was announced.“All the houses are empty because of the migrant plans,” she claimed.“Who would want to move in with this looming over your head?”Another resident, Igor Jelisejevs, 39, moved into an Annington-owned three-bedroom property at The Paddocks in August. His home is close to the former RAF base.“When I moved in I had two neighbours. Five weeks later, it is still the same,” he said.However, Jelisejevs said the proposed plans did not personally concern him.“The plans don’t really bother me. I will be able to look after myself,” he said. “But it is a shame really that people are being put off by the plans.”Residents divided over proposed centreNot all residents share the same concerns.Ayoub Sabir, 33, who lives on Maple Grove, said he was not “bothered” by the proposed arrival of asylum seekers as long as appropriate security measures were in place.“I believe in the security system, and I think we will be safe,” said Sabir, who recently became a father.Meanwhile, 84-year-old Michael Thompson said his family had considered moving but instead decided to install CCTV cameras.A sign outside his home reads: “Asylum Centre: Still the Wrong Place, Wrong Plan.”“It has left people in limbo,” Thompson said.Another resident, a 50-year-old mother of four who moved to the UK from South Africa five years ago, said the prospect of the centre had brought back memories of violence she experienced previously.She said she had been hijacked and had a gun held to her head before moving to the UK.“We came to the UK to escape fear and somewhere our children will be safe,” she said. “But these plans have ruined it for us if they go ahead.”Police warn of potential pressure on resourcesNorth Yorkshire Police has warned that if the government proceeds with the plans, policing protests around the site could require significant resources and potentially put pressure on policing elsewhere in the county.The concerns have also been raised directly with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood by York and North Yorkshire Mayor David Skaith and Deputy Mayor for Policing, Fire and Crime Jo Coles.Martin Sanderson, a prominent member of the Linton-on-Ouse Action Group, accused the Home Office of making the village “inaccessible and unsafe” for residents and families.However, such claims remain part of the ongoing local dispute over the proposed accommodation centre.Council raises concerns over village’s futureSix of the seven North Yorkshire MPs, along with North Yorkshire Council leader Cllr Carl Les OBE, have said they do not believe the former RAF Linton-on-Ouse site is an appropriate location for a large-scale asylum accommodation centre.North Yorkshire Council said there were concerns that the proposed facility could “damage confidence, hinder future regeneration and conflict with wider ambitions for housing, employment and economic growth.”The council was approached for further comment.Annington declined to comment, while the Home Office was also approached for a response.You use AI every day. articles.title: Montana meltdown: MAGA attacks Indians teaching at Montana State University. Turns out they are the 'best of the best'
articles.summary: Social media witnessed a severe Montana meltdown as Montana Governor Greg Gianforte went to India for trade talks.
articles.body: Social media witnessed a severe Montana meltdown as Montana Governor Greg Gianforte went to India for trade talks. While Gianforte got trolled, with some calling for his impeachment too, one social media account went after Indians working at Montana State University, only to get exposed for stupidity as social media users pointed out that all of them are from the top educational instututes of India."Montana State University’s Mechanical/Industrial Engineering Department is headed by a graduate of the Punjab Agricultural University," the account posted from the website of the university. The same screenshot showed that Dilpreet Singh Bajwa, the head of the department, did his MS and PhD in the US, from the University of Illinois."Montana State University’s Dean of the College of Agriculture is a graduate of the Kerala Agricultural University in India," the post said about Sreekala Bajwa. Sreekala did her master's at IIT Kharagpur and then her doctorate from the University of Illinois."Montana State University Professor Shivali Banerjee is a graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology in Bombay," the post said, without knowing the standard of IITs in India."Montana State University Professor Amalesh Jana is a graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati and Jadavpur University," the post said about the fourth person. Jana did his PhD at Oregon State University.While the MAGA account thought these findings to be a great expose, social media users marveled at the foolishness."How's getting into IIT Bombay a bad thing," one wrote."Imagine being so stupid that you think pointing out someone graduating from IIT Bombay is an insult!," another wrote."IIT Bombay is one of the best universities in India, you need to be a really smart student to get into that," a third user wrote."Are you bragging US secured the best of best of india?" one questioned."It's harder to get into IIT Bombay than it is to get into Harvard or MIT," one comment read."I know of an IITB graduate multimillionaire in Silicon Valley whose entire house staff is white Americans. articles.title: National Commission for Women issues safety guidelines to step-up monitoring of app-based and digital transport services
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Taking note of safety concerns emerging from across states the National Commission for Women has issued guidelines to states and UTs for safety
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Taking note of safety concerns emerging from across states the National Commission for Women has issued guidelines to states and UTs for safety of women passengers using app-based and digital transport services calling for appropriate verification of criminal antecedents, police verification and background of drivers before onboarding, monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours and providing SOS buttons in every cab to send out alerts to the command-and-control centre.The NCW notes that as cabs, auto-rickshaws, bike taxis and other app-enabled transport services have become an integral part of everyday mobility, particularly for women travelling independently, ensuring safety throughout the journey has assumed greater importance.Instances relating to mismatch in driver or vehicle identity, route deviation, inappropriate conduct, harassment, stalking, unsafe drop-offs, delays in emergency response and inadequate grievance redressal underline the need for a coordinated and accountable safety framework.The guidelines issued in this backdrop also take into consideration the recommendations of the Justice J S Verma Committee Report, 2013, and the regulatory framework under the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025, issued by the ministry of road transport and highways.NCW chairperosn Vijaya Rahatkar, has written to the chief secretaries of all states and UTs, requesting appropriate measures for implementation of the guidelines.Bringing focus on verification of driver and vehicle, the guidelines lay down that the aggregators shall ensure that the driver and vehicle assigned to a passenger match the details displayed on the application. “Any unauthorised change in the driver or vehicle shall be appropriately flagged in the application and treated as a safety concern,” it asserts. The guidelines also call for mechanisms for real-time alerts for route deviations or suspicious stoppages.The guidelines also call for penalty-free cancellation in case of identity mismatch. The guidelines also lay down that the aggregators must strive to maintain a verified pool of women drivers, enabling women travelling alone with the option to request a woman driver through the application.Calling for enhanced verification and monitoring of drivers operating during late-night hours, the guidelines set out measures ranging from mandatory driver photo verification at trip commencement, addressing driver intoxication, enhanced command and control centre monitoring and a safe-drop option at the end of the ride.“Aggregators may establish a dedicated and time-bound grievance redressal mechanism for complaints relating to driver misconduct, harassment, assault, route deviation, unauthorised driver or vehicle substitution and failure of emergency-response mechanisms,” the guidelines state.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US F-1 visa: Indian student claims October interview date got canceled for refusing to pay agent extra ₹20,000
articles.summary: An Indian student claimed on Reddit that an agent asked for an additional Rs 20,000 for an F-1 visa interview, which the Redditor refused to pay and
articles.body: An Indian student claimed on Reddit that an agent asked for an additional Rs 20,000 for an F-1 visa interview, which the Redditor refused to pay and received a message that the appointment was canceled. The student, who is planning to pursue a programme at a US university, originally had an I-20 showing an August 31, 2026 programme start date. "Unfortunately, I couldn’t get a visa interview appointment before my school start date, so my agent told me the intake would probably have to be moved to January 2027," the student said.According to the student's account, the agent later informed that he had secured an October 19 visa interview appointment. But for that, an additional ₹20,000 was to be paid. "I refused because I wasn't sure why I needed to pay this extra amount. He then told me that if I didn't pay, he would cancel the appointment. He actually cancelled it, and I received the cancellation confirmation," the Reddit post read."Now when I log into the official US visa scheduling website, my application is still showing as “Open” and the post is Mumbai, but there are currently no available appointments. I have not paid my SEVIS fee yet either. My I-20 still shows the old August 31, 2026 start date, although my agent says I should move my studies to January 2027," the student said."I’m worried because I don't know whether I should continue using this agent, try to manage the appointment myself, ask my school for a new I-20 for January, or do something else first. I also don't want to pay ₹20,000 if it's simply an agent's additional charge and not an official visa fee," the post added.What are the official F-1 visa fees?The US Department of State lists the application processing fee for F, M and J visas at $185. Students applying for an F-1 visa are also generally required to pay the I-901 SEVIS fee before the visa can be issued. The SEVIS fee is separate from the visa application fee. There is no standard US government fee described as a ₹20,000 "appointment fee" for an F-1 interview.Getting visa slots through agentsThough USCIS has warned against paying any extra money to any individual or company and called these immigration scams. "IT'S A SCAM: Sometimes businesses and websites pretend to be immigration experts or say they have special connections to the government," USCIS recently posted on social media. "They might also “guarantee” that you can get a visa, Green Card, or work permit faster if you pay a fee."On the USCIS website, they have a full statement on this. "We recognize that the immigration process can be complex and that applicants, petitioners, and requestors are at risk of becoming victims of scams or fraud. We encourage you to use the information on this webpage to help safeguard your information and avoid becoming a victim," it says"You do not need a representative to file forms with USCIS. You may file forms by yourself and represent yourself before USCIS. If you choose to have a representative, make sure the person helping you is an attorney or an accredited representative working for a Department of Justice -recognized organization. Only attorneys or accredited representatives (or certain law students or law graduates working under their supervision) are authorized to represent you on immigration matters before USCIS," it adds.But many Redditors said that only agents are getting visa interview slots and there is no other way to get a slot in such an emergency situation like college admission.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Canadian couple started Aslan Organics with two 8-by-12-foot plots in 2017; nine years later, they own a 50-acre Ontario farm and say their 2.5-acre market garden crossed $200,000 in annual revenue
articles.summary: Discover how Shane and Emma Rozeveld turned their passion for gardening into a thriving business, Aslan Organics, amassing over $200,000 in annual revenue while managing a 50-acre farm in Ontario.
articles.body: Shane and Emma Rozeveld, a Canadian couple who started growing food on two 8-by-12-foot plots, now own a 50-acre farm in Ontario.The couple started Aslan Organics in 2017 at the Yarrow Ecovillage in Chilliwack, British Columbia. They started growing for fun, but as yields grew, so did the business potential.The turning point came when Shane decided to leave his desk job and pursue farming full time.“I really had no idea what I was doing,” Shane said during an episode of the Carrot Cashflow podcast, hosted by Diego Footer.An opportunity soon pushed the couple beyond hobby gardening. Another family at the ecovillage was leaving and offered to sell its market-garden equipment to them, including a greenhouse, cooler, bins, and other infrastructure.Their first commercial operation covered about a third of an acre. They started with basic tools, even cutting greens with scissors, before investing in a greens harvester. Shane said the couple followed a strategy of putting their earnings back into the business to expand the operation.A fresh start in OntarioThe couple moved to Ontario in 2020 and restarted the business in Sarnia in 2021 after taking a year off during the COVID period.Their experience in British Columbia had been rewarding but financially limited. Shane described the farm there as largely cash-neutral, while the market near Vancouver was crowded with established organic growers.Sarnia offered a different opportunity. Shane said the city had about 75,000 people and a farmers' market that operated indoors and outdoors year-round, giving the couple a market that was less constrained by weather.When Shane first approached the Sarnia Farmers' Market, he said he was told, “we just don't do organics at this market”. The couple then had to establish themselves through their produce and regular appearances.Their first market brought in just $247.By August or September, Shane said that figure had grown to about $1,500 per market. Customers were returning for their salad mix, lettuce, arugula, radishes and turnips.“People were like, trying our salad mix. And they're like, I've never had salad mix like this in my life,” Shane said.The business continued to grow year after year. Shane said revenue increased by at least 30% in most years, with one year recording about 40% growth and another doubling.Revenue rose from about $173,000 in 2024 to more than $200,000 in 2025, marking the first time the business crossed the $200,000 threshold, according to Shane.From $247 market days to $10,000 weeksAslan Organics generates revenue through several channels, including farmers' markets, online sales, farm shares and wholesale customers.The scale of the change is evident in the weekly numbers. Shane said a recent early-April weekend brought in more than $2,000 at the market and more than $1,000 through online sales.During the previous summer, there were weeks when the farm generated more than $10,000 in sales through its different channels.“We've gone from $1,000 a week to 10,000 a week in about five years,” Shane said.The farm-share programme has grown alongside the business. Shane said it started with 24 customers, then expanded to 32, more than 40, 60 and 80. The couple were targeting more than 100 customers for the current year.Unlike a traditional fixed vegetable box, customers can choose what they want from the produce available that week. The couple also allow customers to skip some weeks during the summer.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A man went to a furniture auction in England in 1915 and bought Stonehenge for £6,600 on a whim; three years later, he gave the monument to Britain
articles.summary: On 21 September 1915, a British lawyer named Cecil Chubb went to an auction in Salisbury, England, reportedly hoping to buy furniture.
articles.body: On 21 September 1915, a British lawyer named Cecil Chubb went to an auction in Salisbury, England, reportedly hoping to buy furniture. He came home as the owner of Stonehenge, the mysterious Neolithic monument in southern England. According to the History website, his winning bid was six thousand six hundred British pounds. The purchase began as a whim and ended as one of the most generous gifts of heritage in British history, because Chubb handed the stones to the nation. Here is how a furniture trip turned into the strangest property deal.How in 1915, Cecil Chubb attended a Salisbury auction to buy furnitureChubb was born only a few miles from Stonehenge. In 1915, he attended the sale at the Palace Theatre in Salisbury, and the account describes him as someone who went along to pick up furniture. According to History, he went to the auction as he wanted to buy dining chairs.The monument was listed as Lot 15, together with a triangle of neighbouring land of about thirty acres. Both had belonged to the family of Sir Edmund Antrobus. His death in 1915 put the estate on the auction block, so a landmark visited by people from around the world was sold like any other property.A winning bid of 6,600 pounds on a whim, and a wife who expected household itemsChubb won the lot with a bid of six thousand six hundred British pounds. Adjusted for inflation, it says, that is a little more than one million dollars today. For a prehistoric monument that had stood for thousands of years, it was a modest sum.History reports that Chubb said he had not planned to bid on Stonehenge at all. In a newspaper interview, he explained that, once in the room, he felt a Salisbury man ought to buy it. His wife, Mary, reportedly expected him to return with household goods and was less than pleased with the surprise.From private owner to gift: Chubb gave Stonehenge to the nation and became a baronetChubb's ownership lasted only three years. On 26 October 1918, he deeded Stonehenge to the British people as a gift. That gift is why he is remembered as the last private owner of the monument.Prime Minister David Lloyd George rewarded the gift in 1919 by naming him Sir Cecil Chubb, First Baronet of Stonehenge. In the same year, the British government began a major renovation, straightening stones and setting them in concrete.Deed conditions and Stonehenge today, a protected World Heritage Site after a centuryThe deed attached three requirements, according to History. The public would be admitted for a modest fee, the monument would be preserved as closely as possible to its existing state, and new construction nearby would be tightly restricted.Stonehenge now forms part of the World Heritage Site called Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites, designated by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation. Maintenance and preservation of the monument have continued for more than a century since Chubb's gift. The article adds that the stones' purpose and the way they were raised remain open questions.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: India, Switzerland eye deeper ties in trade, investment, tech
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India and Switzerland looked to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, technology, defence production and nuclear energy as PM Modi held
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India and Switzerland looked to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, technology, defence production and nuclear energy as PM Modi held talks with visiting Swiss President Guy Parmelin. The two countries also signed five agreements, including one for a migration and mobility partnership and another for exchange of young professionals.Identifying innovation, infrastructure and advanced technology as strong pillars of the bilateral partnership, Modi said India and Switzerland were going to give the relationship a new momentum and take it to new heights.The two countries set up a committee to facilitate trade and investment and address trade-related concerns, building upon Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) signed between India and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) countries in 2024. TEPA was India's first FTA with any economic bloc in Europe, as Modi recalled."It is also an ambitious blueprint for investment, innovation, jobs, and shared prosperity. Through this, we aim to achieve the targets of $100 billion in investment in India and 1 million direct jobs over the next 15 years," said Modi in his media statement.Key highlights of TEPA included enhanced market access for Indian goods and services, $100 billion investment commitment over 15 years, creation of 1 million jobs in India and stronger bilateral relations with EFTA nations.The leaders discussed the conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia, with the Swiss President welcoming Modi's message to Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war.Modi said India and Switzerland believe in democratic values, the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy and will continue to work together for global peace and stability."Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace," he said, adding that the leaders also agreed that reforms in global institutions are essential to address the growing global challenges.PM said the mobility agreement will open up many new opportunities in Switzerland for Indian students, researchers, professionals and young people. The agreement provides for multiple-entry visas for up to five years, including stays of up to six months on each visit, and renewable one-year student permits.The two sides also signed another MoU to govern exchange of young professionals taking up temporary employment in the other country to enhance their professional and language skills. According to the Indian govt, the MoU incorporates exchange of 300 persons annually per country, which may increase to 500, and a timeline of 30/90 days for verification of nationality/residency status, among other provisions.Modi said both countries had taken several important decisions to increase market access for Indian exports in Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries."This will help increase exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and engineering goods to Switzerland. At the same time, we will attract Swiss investments into key sectors, such as biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing, and sustainability," said Modi.Parmelin said the partnership is mutually beneficial. "India gains from capital, technology transfers, and facilitated access to markets for high-value-added goods. Switzerland, for its part, benefits from exchanges with an immense partner experiencing sustained growth, at a time when global trade has become more exposed and unpredictable," said Parmelin.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1914, a California family bought what became the 6,625-acre Kinsey Ranch; 112 years later, after one brother pushed to protect it before his death, the entire working cattle ranch is now permanently protected from development
articles.summary: The Kinsey family bought a stretch of California countryside in 1914 that would eventually become a 6,625-acre working cattle ranch.
articles.body: The Kinsey family bought a stretch of California countryside in 1914 that would eventually become a 6,625-acre working cattle ranch. After more than a century, the family has taken steps to ensure the property remains protected from development. The place is for cattle, forests, rivers and wildlife rather than new development.The Northcoast Regional Land Trust (NRLT) has completed a conservation easement on the Kinsey Ranch in Benbow, California, according to a report by North Coast Journal. This permanently protects the agricultural, forest and watershed values while allowing the family to continue working it as a ranch.The agreement does not mean the family no longer owns the property. But the easement permanently places restrictions on how the property can be developed, allowing it to remain working land even if it changes hands in the future.A ranch built over generationsIn 1914, Charles and Alice Kinsey bought the land that later became the 6,625-acre Kinsey Ranch. The land sits in Benbow, in southern Humboldt County, along the East Branch of the South Fork Eel River. Their grandson David Johnson became the person at the heart of the conservation effort. Their descendants continued to work the land, and today, more than 4,500 acres of the ranch are used for a cow-calf grazing operation. The property also contains forestland managed for sustainable timber production. But agriculture is only part of what makes the ranch significant.More than five miles of the East Branch of the South Fork Eel River run through the property. There are more than 10 miles of smaller streams. The waterways provide habitat for endangered salmon and other wildlife. The conservation easement placed on the ranch also protects farmland soils, wetlands and riparian habitat, the areas alongside rivers and streams that are particularly important for plants and animals.“It’s a great example of conservation and agricultural communities coming together to keep working lands protected and productive while preserving important habitat for the wildlife that depend on them. We’re grateful to the Kinsey family and our project partners, including the Department of Conservation and Strategic Growth Council, for helping create an outcome that benefits agricultural use, wildlife, and conservation for generations to come,” Zach Wenderott, NRLT Project Manager, said in a release.The family wanted to protect itThe conservation project took years to complete and was driven in part by David Johnson, a member of the family that had owned and worked the ranch for generations. David worked on the ranch since his grandparents, Charles and Alice Kinsey, bought it in 1914. Though David passed away in 2024, prior to the easement’s completion, this was his biggest dream: to protect the land.“My brother really wanted to conserve it. If this hadn’t been funded, our kids couldn’t afford to keep it. But now even if they do sell it, it will be protected as our family had wanted. It’s too gorgeous and big a property to just let go to development,” Marjorie Johnson Yates, whose family has owned the ranch for three generations, told the outlet.The location of the Kinsey Ranch also adds to its conservation value. It is located within a few miles of NRLT's completed Wagner Ranch and Sproul Creek conservation easements. Other projects are also underway nearby. Along with this land, these projects will build a corridor of protected working lands and habitat in the Benbow and Garberville area.“We all know that with time and money, damage to the land can be repaired and restored to its natural state. But it is much better to preserve, rather than to have to restore,” Tom Strobel, who represented the Kinsey family throughout the process, said.The conservation easement closes a chapter that began when the Kinsey family purchased the property more than 110 years ago. The ranch will continue as a working ranch. Cattle can continue to graze its grasslands, timber can continue to be managed and the rivers can continue to run through the property. But its future remains secure. Whether the ranch stays within the family or eventually passes to someone else, the conservation protections will remain. The decision made by one generation has therefore created a lasting safeguard for the generations that follow.Meanwhile, the NRLT plans to honour the Kinsey and Johnson families’ multi-generational dedication to the land during the Boots & Birkenstocks Annual Celebration on 11 October.You use AI every day. articles.summary: DMK candidate I Paranthamen accuses CM Vijay of MLA “horse-trading” ahead of bypolls; TVK denies and asks ECI to disqualify him for poll code violation.
articles.body: Chennai: A day before the bypolls, DMK and TVK traded barbs accusing each other of violating the poll code.Speaking to reporters in Chennai, DMK’s Madurantakam candidate I Paranthamen raked up a complaint of horse-trading against TVK and demanded action against chief minister C Joseph Vijay. Meanwhile, former DMK minister V Senthilbalaji posted pictures of a sari and a lamp on his X handle and alleged that they were being distributed to voters in Dharapuram. While TVK denied the gift distribution charge, the party lodged a complaint against Paranthamen to Election Commission of India, alleging that DMK was ‘campaigning’ during the silent period and making baseless allegations against Vijay. In its complaint submitted to chief electoral officer Archana Patnaik, TVK also sought the disqualification of Paranthamen’s candidature, alleging that he had attempted to “illegally influence” voters in Madurantakam.Paranthamen said that two MDMK MLAs elected on the DMK symbol — T M Rajendran of Kadayanallur and R Senthil Selvan of Sirkazhi — had lodged separate complaints against Vijay to Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) on Oct 1. The complaint alleged that CM sought to lure the two and wanted them to resign from the assembly. But no action had been taken on the complaint so far, said Paranthamen. “If DVAC fails to register a case against Vijay, DMK will initiate legal action against him,” he said. He further alleged that TVK minister Aadhav Arjuna, MDMK general secretary Vaiko and his son Durai Vaiko were a part of the horse-trading attempt.Countering the charge, TVK legal wing representatives said they had petitioned CEO against Paranthamen for “attempting to influence voters through illegal means”. The complaint from Aadhav asked ECI to disqualify Paranthamen’s candidature and said he shouldn’t be allowed into Madurantakam constituency until the counting was over. “The CEO assured of appropriate action,” said a TVK functionary.TVK functionaries denied Senthilbalaji’s voter-bribing charges. The former DMK minister said voters in booth No. 30 of Manoorpalayam in Kundadam west union of Dharapuram assembly segment were given gifts. articles.title: 'Judicial impropriety': Ex-CJI Gavai on sitting SC judge Bhuyan's remarks criticising SIR
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's criticism of deletion of a large number of voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) process, when the issue
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's criticism of deletion of a large number of voters through the special intensive revision (SIR) process, when the issue is pending adjudication before Supreme Court, drew a sharp reaction from former CJI BR Gavai, who termed it judicial impropriety.The former CJI refrained from directly commenting on his former colleague's remarks, but stressed a sitting or retired judge of Supreme Court, high court or any court must not speak on matters that are pending adjudication before a court."I am of the firm view that judicial discipline and propriety do not allow any sitting or retired judge to speak something which pertains to issues pending adjudication before SC, HC or any court," Justice Gavai said when asked by the media about Justice Bhuyan's statement at Nalsar, Hyderabad Sunday on the SIR of electoral rolls.Besides Justice Bhuyan, former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman also criticised the intensive revision of rolls, saying a citizen's right to vote, which is at the heart of democracy, was at "great peril" because of "illegal knocking out" of people from voters' lists.The SIR exercise in West Bengal was challenged before SC, which upheld it after tweaking the process by first engaging judicial officers in the scrutiny of documents and then providing for a special appeal provision by constituting tribunals.However, petitions which challenge SIR in different states, where large-scale deletion of voters from draft rolls has taken place mainly because of "logical discrepancy" and "voter mapping" issues, are still pending in courts.Justice Bhuyan, speaking at Nalsar, had said that any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens is intrinsically arbitrary as it strikes at the heart of the Constitution.Former CJI Gavai said he does not want to comment on Justice Bhuyan's statement.Justice Bhuyan had said, "Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens making them citizens without voting rights would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of the Constitution.""If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary... No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Supreme Court may get 3 judges today, to be one short of full strength
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union law ministry Monday notified appointment of three judges for Supreme Court, taking the total strength of the apex court to 37 judges,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union law ministry Monday notified appointment of three judges for Supreme Court, taking the total strength of the apex court to 37 judges, including Chief Justice of India, against a sanctioned strength of 38 judges. The new judges will take oath of office likely Tuesday.The three new judges for SC are Justice Sunita Agarwal, currently Chief Justice of Gujarat High Court; Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, Chief Justice of Delhi High Court; and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh, Chief Justice of Telangana High Court.The three chief justices were recommended for elevation to the apex court on Sept 28 by the SC collegium, comprising of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Vikram Nath, B V Nagarathna, M M Sundresh and P S Narasimha.Justice Agarwal will be the third woman judge in SC with Justices B V Nagarathna and V Mohana, the other two currently on the bench. While Justices Agarwal and Upadhyay come from the same parent HC of Allahabad, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh's parent HC is Jharkhand.With the latest appointments, Allahabad High Court has four representations on SC bench, the others include Justices Vikram Nath, who will be the next CJI in Feb, and Justice Manoj Mishra.Justice Agarwal and Justice Upadhyay were appointed judges of Allahabad HC in Nov 2011 while Justice Singh was appointed judge of Jharkhand HC in Jan 2012. Justice Agarwal became CJ of Gujarat HC in July 2023. Justice Upadhyay was appointed CJ of Bombay HC on July 29, 2023 and then CJ of Delhi HC on Jan 21, 2025.The law ministry also notified appointment of Saket court judicial officer Gurvinder Pal Singh as additional judge of Delhi HC, a two year tenure before an additional judge is confirmed as permanent judge of the HC.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A man left his tech career to build Harry Potter-inspired cottages in Tennessee; the three-home project cost $700,000 and rents for up to $700 a night
articles.summary: Justin Kersey once worked in technology, building a career as a consultant and delivery manager for companies including UPS, Tractor Supply and S&P Global.
articles.body: Justin Kersey once worked in technology, building a career as a consultant and delivery manager for companies including UPS, Tractor Supply and S&P Global. Then he took a very different route, teaming up with his uncle, Joe McCarthy, to develop fantasy-themed holiday homes in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee. What began with plans for conventional park-model houses eventually became a collection of elaborate properties inspired by fantasy worlds. Their latest project includes three cottages based on characters from Harry Potter, each designed with its own architecture and interiors. As reported by PEOPLE, together, the three cottages cost about $700,000 to build and now attract guests throughout the year.How a technology consultant built Harry Potter-inspired holiday homesKersey's route into the holiday-rental business was not a straightforward change of profession. He studied at Towson University before completing an MBA at Duke University, then worked in technology as a consultant and delivery manager. His employers included UPS, Tractor Supply and S&P Global.Outside his main career, however, he was already considering what else he might do. Kersey and his uncle eventually bought a commercial lot near Pigeon Forge, a Tennessee destination known for its tourism industry, and initially imagined developing more conventional park-model accommodation. The idea changed once they began thinking about how the properties could offer guests something more distinctive.Rather than simply constructing small holiday homes, the pair began building around fantasy settings. Their first major collection consisted of eight properties inspired by The Lord of the Rings. It was their own customers and growing social media audience that helped point them towards the next project. Interest in fantasy-themed accommodation was already visible in the response to the earlier properties, and Kersey and McCarthy decided to apply that approach to the world of Harry Potter.The result was not intended to be a literal recreation of locations from the books or films. Instead, the team imagined what homes belonging to particular characters might look like.Inside the three Harry Potter-inspired fantasy cottagesThe three properties each have a separate identity. The Wizard's Retreat takes inspiration from Harry and Ginny, while the Wizard's Library is based around Hermione Granger. The Wizard's Herbarium, meanwhile, draws from Luna Lovegood. Kersey's team designed the spaces around characteristics associated with each character rather than simply filling the rooms with recognisable references.There are custom bookcases and chandeliers, antique furnishings, sleeping nooks and suspension nets. Other details include potion bottles, miniature fairy settings, gnome displays and murals. Torch-style and fairy lighting is used to alter the feel of the rooms, while the architecture combines Tudor-Gothic elements with influences from the surrounding Appalachian region.Some of the details are easy to miss at first. That was intentional. Kersey says part of the experience is allowing guests to discover smaller pieces of the design as they move through the house. The properties are therefore closer to themed accommodation than ordinary holiday cottages with a few decorative touches added afterwards.The $700,000 project involved months of design and constructionThe design process alone took roughly three to four months for each cottage. Construction then required another six to seven months. Kersey and his team acted as the prime contractor, bringing in subcontractors for specialist stages of the work while staying directly involved in areas such as carpentry. They also took responsibility for the decorating.That hands-on approach came with some practical problems. Parts of the framing did not match the original plans, forcing the team to abandon spiral staircases that had been intended for two of the houses. Those were replaced with conventional staircases. There were smaller headaches too. Kersey recalls that workers collectively spent more than 100 hours searching for tools that had not been returned to their proper places.The three Harry Potter-inspired cottages ultimately cost about $700,000 to build. Custom interior carpentry was the biggest individual expense, reflecting just how much of the design was created specifically for the properties rather than bought off the shelf.The cottages can cost up to $700 a nightThe finished homes are rented at different rates depending on the time of year and the day of the week. Prices range from roughly $250 to $700 per night. Peak dates include Halloween, Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve. Late January and February are generally cheaper, putting the properties into their lower seasonal period.According to the PEOPLE, Kersey says the cottages average about 90% occupancy month to month. Their guests are not limited to dedicated fantasy fans either. Couples celebrating special occasions, families, grandparents travelling with grandchildren and visitors specifically travelling to Pigeon Forge for the experience have all stayed there.The properties have also hosted marriage proposals, anniversaries, birthdays and several small weddings. Across Mountain Shire's fantasy properties, the business has accumulated a 4.97 out of five Airbnb rating from more than 1,800 reviews, according to Kersey.Social media has become part of the businessThe cottages have also developed a substantial online audience. Videos showing the interiors and construction process have attracted millions of views, while guests regularly post their own footage. Kersey said, “We get a lot of bookings directly from social media, particularly Instagram and TikTok, and many guests tell us seeing one of our reels is what convinced them to book.”It gives the properties a marketing advantage that conventional holiday accommodation may not have. The unusual interiors are naturally suited to short-form video, and each room provides something different for visitors to film. For a business built around highly specific visual experiences, social media has effectively become another way of showcasing the houses.More fantasy properties are already plannedMountain Shire's expansion is not stopping with the three cottages. Kersey expects at least two more properties to be added by the middle of 2027. One planned project, called Sanctum Patronus, will take inspiration from Patronuses, with designs incorporating creatures including a white stag, otter, phoenix, horse and cat. The team is also considering properties based on Hagrid and the Weasley family's Burrow.There is an important distinction in how the business describes these projects. The houses are inspired by familiar fantasy stories, but they are not presented as official or licensed reproductions of the fictional locations. They are Mountain Shire's own interpretations, built around the atmosphere and character associations that fans recognise.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: In 1961, Elvis Presley raised $65,000 toward the USS Arizona Memorial; a year later, the 184-foot structure opened above the Pearl Harbor wreck, where more than 900 crewmen remain entombed and oil still leaks
articles.summary: In 1961, Elvis Presley raised $65,000 towards the USS Arizona Memorial, helping support the project that would honour those who died aboard the battleship
articles.body: In 1961, Elvis Presley raised $65,000 towards the USS Arizona Memorial, helping support the project that would honour those who died aboard the battleship at Pearl Harbor. The memorial was completed that year and officially dedicated in 1962. Its 184-foot structure stretches across the sunken USS Arizona.According to National Park Service, the memorial stands above the battleship that became the final resting place for more than 900 of its 1,177 crewmen who died on December 7, 1941. The USS Arizona remains beneath the structure, while the memorial gives visitors a place to remember those who lost their lives during the Pearl Harbor attack.The idea for a memorial emerged during the Second World War. Initial suggestions were made as early as 1943, but it took several years before concrete steps were taken to create a permanent tribute. In 1949, the Territory of Hawaii established the Pacific War Memorial Commission, helping move the idea forward.The site received its first official recognition in 1950. Admiral Arthur Radford, Commander in Chief of the Pacific, ordered a flagpole to be erected over the sunken battleship. On the ninth anniversary of the attack, a commemorative plaque was placed at the base of the flagpole.How the memorial was createdThe plan for a permanent memorial gained further support in 1958, when President Dwight D. Eisenhower authorised its creation. The project was funded through public contributions and private donations. The memorial was completed in 1961, the same year Presley raised $65,000 towards it.Architect Alfred Preis designed the structure. Its shape was intended to represent the story of the attack and what followed. Preis explained that the structure "sags in the center but stands strong and vigorous at the ends, expressing initial defeat and ultimate victory."Preis also said the overall effect was meant to be one of serenity. He explained that "Overtones of sadness have been omitted to permit the individual to contemplate his own personal responses, his innermost feelings."Three sections above the wreckThe USS Arizona Memorial is divided into three main sections- the Entry Room, the Assembly Room and the Shrine Room.The Entry Room welcomes visitors at the start of their visit. The Assembly Room forms the central section and provides space for ceremonies and general observation. It also gives visitors an area for reflection.The Shrine Room is where the names of those who died aboard the USS Arizona are engraved on a marble wall. The names provide a permanent record of the people who lost their lives aboard the battleship.The memorial stretches across the sunken ship below the surface. Visitors can look through its open windows towards the USS Arizona beneath them.The battleship is no longer in commission, but the United States flag continues to fly from a flagpole attached to its severed mainmast. The flag remains a symbol of the ship's continuing legacy.The USS Arizona Memorial honours the people who died aboard the battleship, but its significance extends beyond the ship itself. The National Park Service says the memorial also honours all military personnel who lost their lives in the Pearl Harbor attack.The USS Arizona beneath memorialMore than 900 of the USS Arizona's 1,177 crewmen who died on December 7, 1941, remain entombed in the sunken battleship. The wreck has therefore remained an important part of the memorial site.Oil still leaks from the USS Arizona, linking the memorial above the water to the physical remains of the ship below it. Visitors standing inside the structure can look towards the wreck beneath the surface.The National Park Service describes the memorial as a place of reflection and remembrance. Its white structure spans the battleship and provides visitors with a way to contemplate the attack and the lives lost.Visiting USS Arizona MemorialThe National Park Service facilitates the USS Arizona Memorial programme. Tickets are free, but reservations are required.The previous first-come, first-served ticket distribution programme is no longer available. Visitors who have reservations are asked to arrive at the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center one hour before their ticket time.The programme lasts around 30 to 45 minutes and is offered as a guided tour. The Pearl Harbor National Memorial Theatre, US Navy vessels and USS Arizona Memorial are fully accessible.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
